children.translated_text: He who has in every way destroyed all darkness, and lifted the world from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) —

children.text: tasmai namaskṛtya yathārthaśāstre śāstraṃ pravakṣyāmyabhidharmakośam // VAkK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to that Teacher of truth, I shall expound the treatise, the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> (Treasury of <s>Abhidharma</s>).

children.text: prajñāmalā sānucarābhidharmaḥ tatprāptaye yāpi ca yacca śāstram /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhidharma</s> is stainless <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) together with its accompaniments; also that [practice] for attaining it, and the treatise [describing it].

children.text: tasyārthato 'smin samanupraveśāt sa cā śrayo 'syetyabhidharmakośam // VAkK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Because there is entry into its meaning in this [treatise], and because it is the basis of that [<s>Abhidharma</s>], [this work is called] the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> (Treasury of <s>Abhidharma</s>).

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ pravicayamantareṇa nāsti kleśānāṃ yata upaśāntaye 'bhyupāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without the thorough analysis of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), there is no means for the pacification of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: kleśaiśca bhramati bhavārṇave 'tra lokastaddhetorata uditaḥ kilaiṣa śāstrā // VAkK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: and it is because of afflictions that the world wanders in the ocean of existence — therefore, it is said, this treatise was proclaimed [by the Teacher].
Conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, excluding the path, are with-<s>āsravas</s> (with defilements) and without-<s>āsravas</s>;
they are 'with-<s>āsravas</s>' because the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) 'lie alongside' them.
The without-<s>āsrava</s> [dharmas] are the truth of the path and also the threefold unconditioned.

children.text: ākāśaṃ dvau nirodhau ca tatrākāśamanāvṛtiḥ // VAkK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) and the two cessations — of these, <s>ākāśa</s> is non-obstruction.
<s>Pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation) is the disconnection [from afflictions], each one separately.
The other cessation, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation), is the absolute prevention of arising.
Those conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, moreover, are the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>): form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so forth.

children.text: sa evādhvā kathāvastu saniḥsārāḥ savastukāḥ // VAkK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: They are also the [three] times, the topics of discourse, [the dharmas] with outflows, and those with real existence.
Those that are with-<s>āsravas</s> are the aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>), also called 'with going' [i.e., leading to rebirth].

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayo loko dṛṣṭisthānaṃ bhavaśca te // VAkK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: They are suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the origin (<s>samudaya</s>), 'the world' (<s>loka</s>), the basis for views (<s>dṛṣṭisthāna</s>), and existence (<s>bhava</s>).
<s>Rūpa</s> (form) consists of the five sense-faculties, the five sense-objects, and <s>avijñapti</s> (imperceptible form).
The bases of those [five] cognitions, the sensitive matter (<s>rūpaprasāda</s>) of the eye and the rest.
<s>Rūpa</s> (visible form) is twofold and twentyfold; sound is eightfold; taste
is sixfold; smell is fourfold; and the tangible is elevenfold in nature.
That which continues — whether wholesome or unwholesome — even for one whose mind is distracted,
based on the great elements, is called <s>avijñapti</s> (imperceptible form).
The [great] elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) are the elements of earth, water, fire, and wind.
They are established in the functions of supporting and so forth: hardness, moisture, heat, and movement.
Earth, in common parlance, refers to color and shape;

children.text: āpastejaśca vāyustu dhātureva tathāpi ca // VAkK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: water, fire, and wind [in common parlance] — but [in Abhidharma] it is the element itself that is meant.
The sense-faculties and sense-objects are held to be the ten <s>āyatanas</s> (bases) and <s>dhātus</s> (elements).
<s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) is experience; <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) has the nature of apprehending distinguishing marks.
The <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations) is other than those four [aggregates]; and these three [non-form aggregates]
are designated <s>dharmāyatana</s> and <s>dharmadhātu</s>, together with <s>avijñapti</s> and the unconditioned.

children.text: vijñānaṃ prativijñaptiḥ mana āyatanaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is awareness of each [object]; <s>manas</s> (mind) is also an <s>āyatana</s> (base);

children.text: dhātavaḥ sapta ca matāḥ ṣaḍ vijñānānyatho mahaḥ // VAkK_1.16 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are considered to be seven [sense-consciousness elements]; the six consciousnesses, and also <s>manas</s>.
The immediately preceding and past consciousness of the six [consciousnesses] — that is <s>manas</s> (mind).
For the purpose of establishing the sixth sense-base, the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> are taught.
The complete inclusion of all [dharmas] is by means of one <s>skandha</s>, one <s>āyatana</s>,
and one <s>dhātu</s> — through [their] intrinsic nature and separation from the nature of others.
The unity of <s>dhātu</s> [is established] through birth, domain, cognition, and commonality;

children.text: dvitve 'pi cakṣurādīnāṃ śobhārtha tu dvayodbhavaḥ // VAkK_1.19 //
children.translated_text: even in [their] duality, the arising of the pair [object and consciousness] is for the purpose of clarity of the eye and the rest.
<s>Skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> mean 'heap,' 'gate,' and 'seed' respectively.
The three teachings of <s>skandhas</s> and so forth are due to delusion, [sharpness of] faculties, and preference, in three ways.
Because [feeling and perception] are the root of disputes and the cause of [continued] <s>saṃsāra</s>, and for the sake of sequence,
<s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), from among the mental factors, are established as separate <s>skandhas</s>.
The unconditioned is not stated among the <s>skandhas</s>, because it does not apply; the sequence, moreover, [is determined]
by coarseness, defilement, [being a] vessel, and so forth — from the meaning of the <s>dhātus</s>.
The five [sense-objects are stated] first because they pertain to the present; the four [non-form skandhas] because they pertain to the material.
Otherwise the sequence is according to position, from the farther to the nearer in function.
For the purpose of specification, due to pre-eminence, multiplicity of <s>dharmas</s>, and inclusion of the foremost,
one <s>āyatana</s> is called '<s>rūpa</s>' and one is called '<s>dharma</s>.'
The eighty thousand collections of <s>Dharmaskandhas</s> (aggregates of <s>Dharma</s>) that the Sage proclaimed —
they are speech and name — their inclusion is within form and formations.
Some say the measure of the treatise [determines a <s>Dharmaskandha</s>]; the narrative of <s>skandhas</s> and so forth, one by one;
but the <s>Dharmaskandha</s> is explained as the antidote to a [particular type of] disposition.
Likewise other <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> as appropriate
should be explained, having ascertained their specific characteristics according to what has been stated.
An opening [in matter] is called the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space-element) — it is said to be [characterized by] light and darkness.
The <s>vijñānadhātu</s> (consciousness-element) is consciousness; with-<s>āsravas</s> [dharmas] are the basis of birth.
One [dhātu] here is 'with designation' — <s>rūpa</s> (visible form); ten are 'with resistance' (<s>sapratigha</s>) —

children.text: rūpiṇaḥ avyākṛtā aṣṭau ta evārūpaśabdakāḥ // VAkK_1.29 //
children.translated_text: the material [dhātus]; eight are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — those same [ten] minus the immaterial and sound.
The others are threefold; all obtained in the desire-realm; in the form-realm, fourteen,
minus the elements of smell, taste, nose, tongue, and their respective consciousnesses.
In the formless realm, only the mind-element, dharma-element, and mind-consciousness-element are obtained;

children.text: sāsravānāsravā ete trayaḥ śeṣāstu sāsravāḥ // VAkK_1.31 //
children.translated_text: these three are both with-<s>āsravas</s> and without-<s>āsravas</s>; the rest are only with-<s>āsravas</s>.
The five consciousness-elements possess <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application);
the last three are of three kinds; the rest are devoid of both.
Through the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptualization) of examination and recollection, [dharmas are] non-conceptual;

children.text: tau prajñāmānasī vyagrā smṛtiḥ sarvaiva mānasī // VAkK_1.33 //
children.translated_text: those two [vitarka and vicāra] are, respectively, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and mental [activity] that is active; <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is entirely mental.
Seven consciousness-<s>dhātus</s> have objects (<s>sālambana</s>); and half of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

children.text: navānupāttā te cāṣṭau śabdaśca anye nava dvidhā // VAkK_1.34 //
children.translated_text: Nine are 'not appropriated' (<s>anupātta</s>); those [nine] plus eight plus sound — the other nine are twofold.

children.text: spraṣṭavyaṃ dvividhaṃ śeṣā rūpiṇo nava bhautikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The tangible is twofold; the remaining nine material ones are derivative (<s>bhautika</s>).
A portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> [is also derivative]; of the ten material [dhātus], [some are] accumulated.

children.text: chinatti chidyate caiva bāhyaṃ dhātu catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: The external [material] group of four elements: cuts and is cut,
burns and weighs — thus there is a debate regarding the burner and the weigher.
The five internal [faculties] are of the nature of <s>vipāka</s> (karmic maturation) and <s>upacayika</s> (accumulative); the maturation-born,

children.text: na śabdaḥ apratighā aṣṭau naiḥṣyandika vipākajāḥ // VAkK_1.37 //
children.translated_text: but not sound; eight are without resistance; the outflowing [dharmas] are maturation-born.
The others are threefold; one possesses [real] substance; the last three are momentary.

children.text: cakṣurvijñānadhātvoḥ syāt pṛthak lābhaḥ sahāpi ca // VAkK_1.38 //
children.translated_text: The eye and eye-consciousness elements may be obtained separately or together.
The twelve internal [dhātus], excluding form and the rest and that designated as <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sabhāgaḥ tatsabhāgāśca śeṣāḥ yo na svakarmakṛt // VAkK_1.39 //
children.translated_text: are 'homogeneous' (<s>sabhāga</s>) and 'similar to those' (<s>tatsabhāga</s>); the rest are those which do not perform their own function.

children.text: daśa bhāvanayā heyāḥ pañca ca antyāstrayastridhā /
children.translated_text: Ten are to be abandoned through cultivation; five plus the last three are threefold [to be abandoned];

children.text: na dṛṣṭiheyamakliṣṭaṃ na rūpaṃ nāpyaṣaṣṭhajam // VAkK_1.40 //
children.translated_text: what is not afflicted is not abandoned through [the seeing of] views; nor is form; nor what is born from the sixth [consciousness alone].
Portions of the eye and of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> are 'view' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), which is eightfold.
The <s>dhī</s> (discernment) that arises together with the five consciousnesses is not 'view,' because it does not judge.

children.text: cakṣuḥ paśyati rūpāṇi sabhāgaṃ na tadāśritam /
children.translated_text: The eye sees forms — the homogeneous [eye], not the one upon which [the consciousness] depends.

children.text: vijñānaṃ dṛśyate rūpaṃ na kilāntaritaṃ yataḥ // VAkK_1.42 //
children.translated_text: Consciousness [truly] sees form — for it is not [the case that] an obstructed [form] is seen.
One sees with both eyes, because of the clarity of [binocular] seeing.
The eye, ear, and mind [operate on] objects not in contact; the other three otherwise.
By the three — nose and the rest — the apprehension of an equal [i.e., present] object is held.
The support of the last [manovijñāna] is past; the five [sense-consciousnesses] arise simultaneously with their [supports].
Because they undergo modification through its modification, the eye and the rest are the supports [of consciousness].
Because of this exclusiveness, consciousness is designated by them [i.e., 'eye-consciousness,' etc.].

children.text: na kāyasyādharaṃ cakṣuḥ ūrdhvaṃ rūpaṃ na cakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eye is not below the body, nor is form above the eye;

children.text: vijñānaṃ ca asya rūpaṃ tu kāyasyobhe ca sarvataḥ // VAkK_1.46 //
children.translated_text: and the consciousness of it — but form [is apprehended] on both sides of the body and in all [directions].

children.text: tathā śrotraṃ trayāṇāṃ tu sarvameva svabhūmikam /
children.translated_text: Likewise the ear; for [the objects of] the three [nose, tongue, body], everything belongs to one's own level.
Body-consciousness and the lower level — mind is undetermined [as to level].

children.text: pañca bāhyā divijñeyāḥ nityā dharmā asaṃskṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: The five external [dhātus] are to be known by the gods; the unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> are permanent.

children.text: dharmārdhamindriyaṃ ye ca dvādaśādhyātmikāḥ smṛtāḥ // VAkK_1.48 //
children.translated_text: Half of the <s>dharma</s> [-dhātu] is faculty; and those twelve called 'internal' are remembered [as such].

body.text: abhidharmakośabhāṣye dhātunirdeśo nāma prathamaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośabhāṣya</s>, the exposition of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — the first chapter of the Treasury — is concluded.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and also their cessation — thus speaks the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic).

body.translated_text: This was caused to be written by the glorious <s>Lāmāvaka</s>.

children.translated_text: Over four objects, the supremacy of five [faculties]; over two [objects], [the supremacy]
of groups of four and five and eight — in defilement and purification.
Because of supremacy over the obtaining of one's own object, the six faculties [are each a faculty] for all [dharmas].
But due to supremacy over femininity and masculinity, the female and male faculties [derive] from the body.
Because of supremacy over the abiding in a [rebirth] class, defilement,

children.text: jīvitaṃ vedanāḥ pañca śraddhādyāścendriyaṃ matāḥ // VAkK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: and purification — the life [faculty], the five feelings, and faith and the rest are held to be faculties.
The 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty, the 'knowledge' faculty, and the 'one-who-has-known' faculty likewise —
because of supremacy over progressively higher attainment, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and so forth.
The support of mind, its differentiation, its stability, and defilement itself,

children.text: saṃbhāro vyavadānaṃ ca yāvatā tāvadindriyam // VAkK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: the requisites [of the path], and purification — the faculties are as many as these.
From the support, arising, stability, and experience of activity —
fourteen; and likewise the other faculties [derive] from cessation.
The pain-faculty (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>) is the unpleasant bodily feeling; happiness (<s>sukha</s>)

children.text: śātā dhyāne tṛtīye tu caitasī sā sukhendriyam // VAkK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: is the pleasant [bodily feeling]; but in the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), that mental [pleasant feeling] is the pleasure-faculty.

children.text: anyatra sā saumanasyaṃ aśātā caitasī punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Elsewhere, that [mental pleasant feeling] is <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure); and the unpleasant mental [feeling]

children.text: daurmanasyamupekṣā tu madhyā ubhayī avikalpanāt // VAkK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: is <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure); <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is the middle [feeling], belonging to both [bodily and mental], because it is non-discriminating.
On the paths of seeing, cultivation, and the adept — nine, three, and three are the stainless [faculties];

children.text: rūpīṇi jīvitaṃ duḥkhe sāsravāṇi dvidhā nava // VAkK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: the material ones, the life [faculty], and the pain [faculty] are with-<s>āsravas</s>; nine are twofold.
<s>Vipāka</s> (maturation) is the life [faculty], twofold; twelve, excluding the last eight,

children.text: daurmanasyācca tattvekaṃ savipākaṃ daśa dvidhā // VAkK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: and <s>daurmanasya</s>; that [life-faculty] is one; with maturation, ten are twofold.
Mind, the other feelings, and faith and the rest — the group of eight — are wholesome in two ways;

children.text: daurmanasyaṃ mano 'nyā ca vittistredhā anyadekadhā // VAkK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>daurmanasya</s>, mind, and the other feeling[s] are threefold; the other [faculties are] one way.
Obtained in the desire-realm, excluding the stainless [faculties]; obtained in the form-realm, [excluding] the female and male faculties

children.text: duḥkhe ca hitvā ārūpyāptaṃ sukhe cāpohya rūpi ca // VAkK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: and the pain [faculty]; obtained in the formless realm, [excluding] the pleasure [faculty] and also the material.
The trio of mind and the two feelings are threefold; <s>daurmanasya</s> is to be abandoned in two ways;

children.text: nava bhavanayā pañca tvaheyānyapi na trayam // VAkK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: nine are [abandoned] through cultivation; five are not to be abandoned; and also the three [stainless faculties are not to be abandoned].
In the desire-realm, at first, maturation of two is obtained; not by spontaneously-born beings;

children.text: teḥ ṣaḍ vā sapta vā aṣṭau vā ṣaḍ rūpeṣu ekamuttare // VAkK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: by them, six, or seven, or eight; in the form-realm, six; in the higher [formless realm], one.
In cessation [attainment], having ceased activity, in the formless realm, the life [faculty], mind,

children.text: upekṣāṃ caiva rūpe 'ṣṭau kāme daśa navāṣṭau vā // VAkK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: and equanimity [cease]; in the form realm, eight; in the desire realm, ten, or nine, or eight.

children.text: kramamṛtyau tu catvāri śubhe sarvatra pañca ca /
children.translated_text: At gradual death, four; everywhere, five wholesome [faculties];
the attainment of nine [faculties] at the last two fruits, with seven, eight, or nine [faculties] for the two [pairs].
<s>Arhatva</s> (arhatship) is [attained] with eleven; but it is said that it can occur with one [additional].
One endowed with equanimity, life, and mind necessarily possesses three.
With four [faculties], one possessing the pleasure and body [faculties]; with five, one possessing the eye and the rest;

children.text: saumanasyī ca duḥkhī tu saptabhiḥ strīndriyādimān // VAkK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: and one with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure); but one with pain possesses seven; one with the female faculty and the rest,
eight; with eleven, one endowed with the 'knowledge' and 'one-who-has-known' faculties.
One endowed with the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty possesses thirteen.
One without merit, with the fewest [faculties], possesses eight — excluding [all] but sensation, mind, body [faculties], and life;
an immature person likewise; in the formless realm, [one possesses] equanimity, life, mind, and the wholesome [faculties].
One endowed with the most possesses nineteen, excluding the stainless [faculties];
one of dual sex; a noble one with passion, [possesses] one sex and the two stainless [faculties] excluded.
In the desire realm, an atom without sound has eight substances, without a faculty;
one with the body-faculty has nine substances; one with another faculty has ten substances.
Mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caittas</s>) necessarily always [arise] together, with all conditioned characteristics;

children.text: prāptyā vā pañcadhā caittā mahābhūmyādibhedataḥ // VAkK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: or [the mental factors are] fivefold, through the division of the great ground (<s>mahābhūmi</s>) and the rest, by means of [their] association.

children.text: vedanā cetanā saṃjñā cchandaḥ sparśo matiḥ smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>cetanā</s> (volition), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>chandas</s> (desire-to-act), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>mati</s> (intellect), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),
<s>manaskāra</s> (attention), and <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)—[these are] in every mind. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.24 //
Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), non-heedlessness (<s>apramāda</s>), tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), shame (<s>hrī</s>), embarrassment (<s>apatrapā</s>),

children.text: mūladvayamahiṃsā ca vīryaṃ ca kuśale sadā // VAkK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: the two roots [of non-attachment and non-hatred], non-harmfulness (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), and vigor (<s>vīrya</s>)—always in the wholesome. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.25 //
Delusion (<s>moha</s>), heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), and restlessness (<s>uddhava</s>)—
always in the defiled; but shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of embarrassment (<s>anapatrapā</s>)—in the unwholesome. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.26 //
Anger (<s>krodha</s>), enmity (<s>upanāha</s>), hypocrisy (<s>śāṭhya</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), harmfulness (<s>pradāsa</s>), concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>),
deceit (<s>māyā</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), and injury (<s>vihiṃsā</s>)—[these are] of the limited-defilement (<s>parīttakleśa</s>) category. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.27 //
Because of being with <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), in a wholesome desire-realm mind,
there are twenty-two mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>); remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) is additional in some [cases]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.28 //
But in the unwholesome that is specifically (<s>āveṇika</s>) [unwholesome] and in that conjoined with views—twenty;
with the four defilements, anger and so forth, [and] remorse—twenty-one. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.29 //
In the indeterminate-obscured (<s>nivṛta</s>) [mind]—eighteen; elsewhere twelve [are] considered in the indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>);

children.text: middhaṃ sarvāvirodhitvādyatra syādadhikaṃ hi tat // VAkK_2.30 //
children.translated_text: sleep (<s>middha</s>), because it is not incompatible with anything, [may be] additional wherever it exists. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.30 //
Remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), sleep (<s>middha</s>), and the unwholesome [factors] do not exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>; therefore,
in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> [is absent] also; and <s>vicāra</s> too beyond that. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.31 //
<s>Āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) is lack of respect for wrongdoing; <s>apatrapā</s> (embarrassment) is the appearance of fear;

children.text: prema śraddhā gurutvaṃ hrīḥ te punaḥ kāmarūpayoḥ // VAkK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: love is faith (<s>śraddhā</s>); respect is <s>hrī</s> (shame); they [belong to] the desire and form [realms]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.33 //
<s>Vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are coarseness and subtlety [of mind]; <s>māna</s> (pride) is self-elevation;

children.text: madaḥ svadharme raktasya paryādānaṃ tu cetasaḥ // VAkK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>mada</s> (intoxication) is the mental inflation (<s>paryādāna</s>) of one attached to his own qualities. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.33 //
<s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are one in meaning; <s>citta</s> and <s>caitasas</s> (mental factors)
share basis, object, and aspect, and are associated in five ways. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.34 //
The <s>viprayukta</s> (dissociated) <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are: <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition), <s>aprāpti</s> (non-acquisition), <s>sabhāgatā</s> (homogeneous nature),

children.text: āsaṃjñikaṃ samāpattī jīvitaṃ lakṣaṇāni ca // VAkK_2.35 //
children.translated_text: the unconscious state (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>), the two attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), life-force (<s>jīvita</s>), and the characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.35 //
<s>Nāmakāya</s> (name-group) and so forth—thus; <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition) is obtaining (<s>lābha</s>) and possession (<s>samanvaya</s>);
<s>prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> [are] of those [dharmas] that have fallen into one's own continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>); of the two cessations— // <s>VAkK</s> 2.36 //
of [dharmas] in the three times—threefold; of the wholesome and so forth—[respectively] wholesome and so forth;
of one's own realm; of those obtained—[prāpti is] fourfold for those not obtained. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.37 //
Threefold, not [belonging to] learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) [categories]; of those not to be abandoned—twofold is accepted;

the <s>avyākṛta</s> (indeterminate) acquisition is co-arisen (<s>sahaja</s>)—except [that obtained] through <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge) and creation (<s>nairmāṇika</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.38 //

children.text: nivṛtasya ca rūpasya kāme rūpasya nāgrajā /
children.translated_text: And of obscured form in the desire realm, not the supreme; of form [in general]—
the non-afflicted indeterminate non-acquisition, of past and unborn [dharmas]—threefold. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.39 //
The non-acquisition of the path is asserted for those who have obtained the stainless [dharmas] of the desire realm and above;
the state of an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjanatva</s>) is that [non-]acquisition; it is lost through traversal across stages. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.40 //
<s>Sabhāgatā</s> (homogeneous nature) is the similarity among beings; the unconscious state (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>), among the unconscious beings,
is the cessation of <s>citta</s> and <s>caittas</s>; [it is] a maturation (<s>vipāka</s>); they [are reborn in] the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> [heaven]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.41 //
Likewise the unconscious attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, with the desire for escape;
it is wholesome, maturing in the next life only; it is not [obtainable] by a noble one (<s>ārya</s>); [it is] a single-time (<s>ekādhvika</s>) acquisition. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.42 //
That called 'cessation' (<s>nirodha</s>) [attainment] is likewise; [it is] for the purpose of dwelling; [it belongs to] the <s>bhavāgra</s> (peak of existence);

children.text: śubhā dvivedyāniyatā ca āryasya āpyā prayogataḥ // VAkK_2.43 //
children.translated_text: wholesome; of two-life [duration]; unfixed; it is obtained by a noble one, through practice (<s>prayoga</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.43 //
Obtainable [only] at awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), not before, by the Sage; from the acquisition of the thirty-fourth moment;
based in one who belongs to the desire or form realm; [obtainable only] among humans, from the cessation attainment first. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.44 //
Lifespan (<s>āyus</s>) is the life-force (<s>jīvita</s>), the support of warmth (<s>ūṣman</s>) and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>)—that which
the characteristics are: birth (<s>jāti</s>), aging (<s>jarā</s>), duration (<s>sthiti</s>), and impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.45 //
Birth of birth (<s>jātijāti</s>) and so forth belong to them; they [operate as] eight dharmas [on] a single [dharma];
birth is the producer of the produced; not without causes and conditions. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.46 //
<s>Nāmakāya</s> (name-groups) and so forth are called collections of designations, sentences, and syllables;
obtained in the desire and form [realms]; called 'being' (<s>sattva</s>); outflow (<s>niḥṣyanda</s>); indeterminate; likewise. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.47 //

children.text: sabhāgatā sā tu punarvipāko 'pi āptayo dvidhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sabhāgatā</s>, however—that is also maturation (<s>vipāka</s>); acquisitions are twofold;

children.text: lakṣaṇāni ca niḥṣyandāḥ samāpattya samanvayāḥ // VAkK_2.48 //
children.translated_text: and the characteristics are outflows; the attainments [are] possessions (<s>samanvaya</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.48 //
<s>Kāraṇa</s> (efficient cause), <s>sahabhū</s> (co-existent), <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous), <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> (conjoined),
<s>sarvatraga</s> (universal), and that called <s>vipāka</s> (maturation)—the cause (<s>hetu</s>) is accepted as sixfold. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.49 //
The <s>kāraṇa</s> (efficient) cause is [all dharmas] other than itself; the <s>sahabhū</s> (co-existent) [causes are] those that are mutual fruits—
like the great elements (<s>bhūta</s>), like mind and mental factors, like a characteristic and its characterized. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.50 //

children.text: caittā dvau saṃvarau teṣāṃ cetaso lakṣaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>caittas</s> (mental factors), the two restraints (<s>saṃvara</s>), their [corresponding] mental characteristics,
and those that follow mind—[are co-existent causes, established] by time, fruit, and other [criteria of] wholesomeness, etc. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.51 //
The <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous) cause [consists of] similar [dharmas], arising from one's own category, [which are] prior;
one another—but in nine stages; the path [serves as homogeneous cause] for [dharmas of] equal and superior [degrees]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.52 //
Those born from practice (<s>prayogaja</s>)—only for those of their own [kind]: those born from hearing, reflection, etc.;
the <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> (conjoined) cause, however—<s>citta</s> and <s>caittas</s> sharing [the same] basis. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.53 //
That called <s>sarvatraga</s> (universal)—of the defiled [dharmas], the prior universals in one's own stage;
the <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) cause is the unwholesome and the wholesome that is defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.54 //
The universal and homogeneous [causes] pervade two times; three [causes] pervade three times;

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ savisaṃyoga phalaṃ nāsaṃskṛtasya te // VAkK_2.55 //
children.translated_text: the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), together with disconnection—[these are] the fruit; not of the unconditioned are those [causes]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.55 //
The maturation fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>) [belongs to] the last [cause]; the dominant fruit (<s>adhipataphala</s>) [belongs to] the first;
the outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) [fruit belongs to] the homogeneous and universal; the personal-effort fruit (<s>pauruṣa</s>) [belongs to] both [kāraṇa and sahabhū]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.56 //
Maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) is an indeterminate dharma, called 'sentient being' (<s>sattva</s>), arising from the determinate [wholesome or unwholesome];

children.text: niḥṣyando hetusadṛśaḥ visaṃyogaḥ kṣayo dhiyā // VAkK_2.57 //
children.translated_text: the outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) resembles its cause; disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) [is] destruction [achieved] through wisdom. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.57 //
That which arises by the force of whatever—that is the fruit born of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>);
it is novel; only of the conditioned; the conditioned [is] the dominant fruit (<s>adhipati</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.58 //

children.text: varttamānāḥ phalaṃ pañca gṛṇhanti dvau prayacchataḥ /
children.translated_text: Five [causes] in the present seize [their] fruit; two give [their fruit from the present];
two [give their fruit when they are] present or past; one [gives] only from the past. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.59 //
The defiled, those born from maturation, and the rest, [and] the first noble [moment]—in due order,

children.text: vipākaṃ sarvagaṃ hitvā tau sabhāgaṃ ca śeṣajāḥ // VAkK_2.60 //
children.translated_text: excluding maturation and universal, those two and homogeneous—[these are the causes] for the remaining [dharmas]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.60 //
<s>Citta</s> and <s>caittas</s>, and others too—excluding the conjoined [cause];

children.text: catvāraḥ pratyayā uktāḥ hetvākhyaḥ pañca hetavaḥ // VAkK_2.61 //
children.translated_text: four conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>) are stated; the one called 'causal' (<s>hetu</s>) [comprises] five causes. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.61 //
<s>Citta</s> and <s>caittas</s>, non-final, [when] arisen—[constitute] the immediately-preceding (<s>samanantara</s>) [condition];
the object-condition (<s>ālambana</s>) is all dharmas; that called <s>kāraṇa</s> (efficient) is remembered as the dominant (<s>adhipati</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 2.62 //

children.text: nirudhyamāne kāritraṃ dvau hetū kurutaḥ trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When ceasing, [a dharma] performs activity; two causes function [in the present]; three [conditions function in the present];

children.text: jāyamāne tato 'nyau tu pratyayau tadviparyayāt // VAkK_2.63 //
children.translated_text: but when arising—the other two conditions [function], and the reverse [of the above]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.63 //
<s>Citta</s> and <s>caittas</s> arise from four [conditions]; the two attainments [arise] from three;

children.text: dvābhyāmanye tu jāyante neśvarādeḥ kramādibhiḥ // VAkK_2.64 //
children.translated_text: others arise from two; not from <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and so forth, nor from sequence and so forth. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.64 //

children.text: dvidhā bhūtāni taddhetuḥ bhautikasya tu pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: The [great] elements are twofold as causes of derived [matter]; but [as cause] of derived matter (<s>bhautika</s>)—fivefold;
derived matter [is] threefold [as cause] of one another; of the great elements—only onefold. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.65 //
In the desire [realm], wholesome and unwholesome; obscured and unobscured mind;
in the form and formless [realms]—other than the unwholesome; the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) is twofold. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.66 //

children.text: kāme nava śubhāccittāccittāni aṣṭābhya eva tat /
children.translated_text: In the desire [realm], from a wholesome mind—nine [types of] minds [arise]; from that—eight exactly;
from ten—the unwholesome; from that—four; the obscured (<s>nivṛta</s>) likewise. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.67 //
From five—the unobscured; from that—seven minds immediately [follow];

children.text: rūpe daśaikaṃ ca śubhāt navabhyastadanantaram // VAkK_2.68 //
children.translated_text: in the form [realm]—ten and one from the wholesome; from nine—that immediately [follows]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.68 //

children.text: aṣṭābhyo nivṛtaṃ tasmāt ṣaṭ tribhyo 'nivṛtaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: From eight—the obscured; from that—six; from three—the unobscured, again—

children.text: tasmāt ṣaṭ evāmārūpye tasya nītiḥ śubhātpunaḥ // VAkK_2.69 //
children.translated_text: from that—six exactly; in the formless, its pattern [is]: from the wholesome, again— // <s>VAkK</s> 2.69 //

children.text: nava cittāni tat ṣaṇṇāṃ nivṛtātsapta tattathā /
children.translated_text: nine minds; that [arises from] six; from the obscured—seven; that likewise—

children.text: caturbhyaḥ śaikṣam asmāttu pañca aśaikṣaṃ tu pañcakāt // VAkK_2.70 //
children.translated_text: from four; the learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) [mind arises] from this; from that—five; the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>)—from five. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.70 //
From that—four minds; these twelve [are] twenty [in total];

children.text: prāyogikopapattyāptaṃ śubhaṃ bhittvā triṣu dvidhā // VAkK_2.71 //
children.translated_text: the wholesome, divided into practice-born (<s>prāyogika</s>) and rebirth-obtained (<s>aupapattyāpta</s>), becomes twofold in the three [realms]. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.71 //
The maturation-born, the path-of-activity, the artisanal, and the positional-and-created—
the indeterminate is fourfold in the desire [realm]; in the form [realm], excluding the artisanal. // <s>VAkK</s> 2.72 //

children.text: kliṣṭe traidhātuke lābhaḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dvayoḥ śubhe /
children.translated_text: In the defiled [state] across the three realms, acquisition of six and six; in the wholesome, [acquisition] of two;

children.text: trayāṇāṃ rūpaje śaikṣe caturṇāṃ tasya śeṣite // VAkK_2.73 //
children.translated_text: of three, born in the form [realm]; in the learner's [state], of four; in the remainder of that [non-learner's state]— // <s>VAkK</s> 2.73 //

body.text:
abhidharmakośe indriyanirddeśo nāma dvitīyaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti /
śrīlāmāvākasya
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, entitled 'Exposition on Faculties' (<s>Indriyanirdeśa</s>). // Of <s>Śrīlāmāvākasya</s>

children.translated_text: Hell-beings, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), animals, humans, [and] six [classes of] celestial beings—
[comprise] the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>); it [has] twenty [divisions] by the distinction of hells and continents. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.1 //
Above, with seventeen levels, is the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), separately [divided]:—

children.text: dhyānaṃ tribhūmikaṃ tatra caturthaṃ tvaṣṭabhūmikam // VAkK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: each <s>dhyāna</s> [has] three levels; but the fourth [has] eight levels. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.2 //
The formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) has no [spatial] location; by rebirth it is fourfold;

children.text: nikāyaṃ jīvitaṃ cātra niśritā cittasantatiḥ // VAkK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: the mind-continuum (<s>cittasantati</s>) therein relies on the [community of] category (<s>nikāya</s>) and life-force (<s>jīvita</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 3.3 //
The destinies (<s>gati</s>), named after hell and so forth, are five; among them, those [beings]
are only undefiled-indeterminate, called 'sentient being' (<s>sattva</s>); not the intermediate being (<s>antarābhava</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 3.4 //
[Beings with] diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, [those with] diverse bodies and uniform perception,
and the reverse—[those with] uniform body and perception; and the formless—these [are] three [and four]. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.5 //
The stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>) are seven; the rest is like a subdivision thereof;
the <s>bhavāgra</s> (peak of existence) and the unconscious beings (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>)—the abodes of beings (<s>sattvāvāsa</s>) are remembered as nine. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.6 //
Because of unwillingness and habituation, [they are] not other [than the seven]; the four stations (<s>sthiti</s>), again,

children.text: catvāraḥ sāsravāḥ skandhāḥ svabhūmāveva kevalam // VAkK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: [consist of] the four defiled <s>skandhas</s>—only in one's own stage. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.7 //

children.text: vijñānaṃ na sthitiḥ proktaṃ catuṣkoṭi tu saṃgrahe /
children.translated_text: Consciousness is not stated [as] a station [of consciousness]; but in the collection [of all dharmas, there is] a fourfold classification;
the four types of birth (<s>yoni</s>) therein, of beings, are egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>) and so forth. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.8 //
Humans and animals [are born in] four ways; hell-beings [are] spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>);
intermediate beings and <s>devas</s> too; <s>pretas</s> also [include] womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 3.9 //
That which exists here between death-existence (<s>mṛtyubhava</s>) and rebirth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>)—
because it has not reached the place of destination, it is called the 'intermediate being' (<s>antarābhava</s>), not yet reborn. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.10 //
From the analogy of the rice-plant continuum, arising of uninterrupted existence;
the reflection [analogy] is unestablished; from dissimilarity it is not a demonstration. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.11 //
Because of the absence of two [in one place] simultaneously; because of the arising of two from what has no continuum;
[the intermediate being] exists—from the statement 'at the throat' [about the] <s>gandharva</s>; from the five[-gati] statement in the <s>sūtra</s> on destiny. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.12 //
From a single projection—it would not reach [otherwise]; [it has] the form of the previous-time existence;
it [arises], moreover, after death, [and exists] before the moment of rebirth. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.13 //
Visible to those of the same class and to the pure divine eye; possessing the speed of <s>karma</s> and <s>ṛddhi</s>;

children.text: sakalākṣaḥ apratighavān anivartyaḥ sa gandhabhuk // VAkK_3.14 //
children.translated_text: with complete sense-faculties, unobstructed, irreversible—it is a feeder on odors (<s>gandhabhuk</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 3.14 //
With inverted understanding it goes to the place of [its] destiny, through desire for pleasure;
another, desiring the smell of [a] place; but [the one headed for] hell [goes] headfirst. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.15 //
One enters [the womb] with full awareness; another also remains [aware]; another
also exits [with awareness]; but another is confused at all [stages]—[this last is the] egg-born. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.16 //
The three [modes of] womb-entry are [respectively] for <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs) and <s>svayaṃbhūs</s> (self-arisen ones);
[the clarity results] from <s>karma</s>, knowledge, or both—from the clarity [thereof], in due order. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.17 //
There is no self (<s>ātman</s>); it is merely <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), conditioned by defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) and <s>karma</s>;
by the continuity of the intermediate being, [the stream] enters the womb—like a lamp. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.18 //
As projected, the continuum grows gradually through defilements and <s>karma</s>;
it goes again to the other world—thus [rotates] the beginningless wheel of existence (<s>bhavacakra</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 3.19 //
That is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), twelve-membered, of three sections (<s>kāṇḍa</s>);
in the prior and later [lives]—two and two; in the middle [life]—eight, completing [the cycle]. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.20 //
The prior defilements [constitute] the ten [types of] <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are prior <s>karma</s>;
the junction-<s>skandhas</s> (<s>saṃdhiskandhāḥ</s>) are consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>); <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) [comes] after that. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.21 //
Before the arising of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>)—that precedes; before the conjunction of the triad—
[there is] contact (<s>sparśa</s>); before the capacity to know the cause of pleasure, pain, etc.— // <s>VAkK</s> 3.22 //
feeling (<s>vedanā</s>); before sexual union—craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>); of one attached to enjoyments and intercourse—

children.text: upādānaṃ tu bhogānāṃ prāptaye paridhāvataḥ // VAkK_3.23 //
children.translated_text: grasping (<s>upādāna</s>) is the running about for the obtainment of enjoyments. // <s>VAkK</s> 3.23 //

children.text: sa bhaviṣyat bhavaphalaṃ kurute karma tat bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: He performs action that will produce the fruit of [future] existence (<s>bhavaphala</s>)—that is <s>bhava</s> (becoming);
<s>pratisaṃdhi</s> (relinking) is rebirth; <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death) is sensation. // VAkK_3.24 //
This [twelvefold chain] pertains to [different] states; it is defiled — but the mention of limbs is due to predominance,
for the removal of confusion regarding the past, the future, and the middle [periods]. // VAkK_3.25 //

children.text: kleśāstrīṇi dvayaṃ karma sapta vastu phalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kleśas</s> (defilements) are three, action is two, <s>vastu</s> (basis) is seven, and fruit likewise;
the condensation into fruit and cause [is established] by inference from the middle of the two [extremes]. // VAkK_3.26 //

children.text: kleśāt kleśaḥ kriyā caiva tato vastu tataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: From defilement arises defilement and action; from that arises <s>vastu</s> (basis); from that again

children.text: vastu kleśāśca jāyante bhavāṅgānāmayaṃ nayaḥ // VAkK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: arise <s>vastu</s> (basis) and defilements — this is the method of the limbs of existence. // VAkK_3.27 //
Herein, the cause is <s>samutpāda</s> (origination); that which has originated is considered the fruit.
The <s>dharma</s> opposed to <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is distinct — <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is like an enemy, falsehood, and so forth. // VAkK_3.28 //
Because of the statement 'fetters and so on,' [it would be] wrong understanding — not so, because of [its being] a view,
because view is associated with it, and because of the teaching that <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is a defilement. // VAkK_3.29 //

children.text: nāma tvarūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ sparśāḥ ṣaṭ saṃnipātajāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nāma</s> (name) is the immaterial <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); the six <s>sparśas</s> (contacts) arise from the conjunction [of three];
five are <s>pratigha-saṃsparśa</s> (contact through impingement); the sixth is called <s>adhivacana-saṃsparśa</s> (contact through designation). // VAkK_3.30 //
<s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and the other contacts [are respectively] undefiled, defiled, and the remainder;
<s>vyāpāda</s> (ill-will) and <s>anunaya</s> (attachment) contacts — the three [feelings] beginning with pleasant feeling [arise from them]. // VAkK_3.31 //

children.text: tajjāḥ ṣaḍvedanāḥ pañca kāyikī caitasī parā /
children.translated_text: Born from those are the six <s>vedanās</s> (feelings); five are bodily, the other is mental;
and further, that [feeling] is of eighteen kinds, through <s>manopavicāra</s> (mental examinations). // VAkK_3.32 //
In the desire realm, all [eighteen] have their own objects; in the form realm, twelve are the domain;
of the three [feelings], the higher [equanimity] — in the two <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), twelve [examinations] pertain to the desire realm. // VAkK_3.33 //

children.text: svo 'ṣṭālambanam ārūpyo dvayoḥ dhyānadvaye tu ṣaṭ /
children.translated_text: One's own [domain] has eight objects in the formless realm; in the two <s>dhyānas</s>, six for the two;

children.text: kāmāḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ caturṇā svaḥ ekasyālambanaṃ paraḥ // VAkK_3.34 //
children.translated_text: in the desire realm, six have four as their own; the object of one is the other. // VAkK_3.34 //
Four in the formless realm border on the form realm; one goes upward;

children.text: eko maule svaviṣayaḥ sarve 'ṣṭādaśa sāsravāḥ // VAkK_3.35 //
children.translated_text: one at the root has its own domain; all eighteen are <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows). // VAkK_3.35 //

children.text: uktaṃ ca vakṣyate cānyat atra tu kleśā iṣyate /
children.translated_text: What has been stated and what will be stated elsewhere — here, the defilement [aspect] is intended.
Like a seed, like the trunk of a <s>nāga</s>-tree, like a root-tree, like a husk, // VAkK_3.36 //
like husk and rice, action is likewise like a medicinal plant and flower;
<s>vastu</s> (basis) is like prepared food and drink — in those four types of existence. // VAkK_3.37 //
<s>Upapattibhava</s> (existence at rebirth) is defiled by all defilements belonging to one's own level;

children.text: tridhānye traya ārūpye āhārasthitikaṃ jagat // VAkK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: the other three are threefold; in the formless realm — the world subsists on <s>āhāra</s> (nutriment). // VAkK_3.38 //
<s>Kavaḍīkāra āhāra</s> (morsel-food) exists in the desire realm, consisting of three <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases);
not the <s>rūpāyatana</s> (form sense-base), because that does not support one's own sense-organ or what it appropriates. // VAkK_3.39 //
<s>Sparśa</s> (contact), <s>cetanā</s> (volition), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are [the other three] nutriments, with-<s>āsravas</s> (outflows) in all three [realms];
<s>manomaya</s> (mind-made) and seeking existence — the <s>gandharva</s> is the intermediate existence. // VAkK_3.40 //
And cessation here is for the purpose of nourishment; of the support and the supported, the pair —
the pair is for the purpose of projecting and ceasing further existence, respectively. // VAkK_3.41 //
Cutting off, reconnecting, dispassion, deterioration, dying, and rebirth —
these are held to be in <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) alone; dying and arising [occur] in <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). // VAkK_3.42 //
These two [dying and arising] do not occur in one-pointed mind or in the two [states of] <s>nirvṛtti</s> (cessation) and <s>avyākṛta</s> (indeterminate);
sequential death [occurs] at the feet, navel, and heart — [this is] the departure of mind. // VAkK_3.43 //
For those born below, humans, gods, and elephants — the cutting of the vital point is by water and so forth;
those determined for the right and wrong [paths] are <s>āryas</s> (noble ones) and those who have committed <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous acts). // VAkK_3.44 //
There, regarding the arrangement of the receptacle-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>), they say: below,
the wind-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) extends upward sixteen hundred thousand [<s>yojanas</s>], immeasurable [in circumference]. // VAkK_3.45 //
The water [circle] extends upward eleven hundred and twenty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>];
eight hundred thousand in height — the rest becomes gold. // VAkK_3.46 //
Laterally, three thousand, four hundred and fifty
and twelve hundred thousand — [such is] the water and gold <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle). // VAkK_3.47 //
The circumference, however, is three times that. There, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Yugandhra</s>,
<s>Īśādhāra</s>, <s>Khadiraka</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s> mountain, // VAkK_3.48 //
<s>Aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>Vinataka</s>, and <s>Nimindhara</s> mountain;

children.text: dvīpāḥ bahiścakravāḍaḥ sapta haimāḥ sa āyasaḥ // VAkK_3.49 //
children.translated_text: the continents beyond, and <s>Cakravāḍa</s> — seven are golden, and it [<s>Cakravāḍa</s>] is of iron. // VAkK_3.49 //
<s>Meru</s> is made of four precious substances; in the water, eighty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>]
submerged; above the water, <s>Meru</s> is again eighty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>]. // VAkK_3.50 //
Half-by-half diminution in the eight [mountain ranges]; and they are equal in height and breadth;
the seven intervals between them are cold [lakes] — the first is eighty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>]. // VAkK_3.51 //

children.text: ābhyantaraḥ samudro 'sau triguṇaḥ sa tu pārśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: That inner ocean — its circumference, however, is three times [its breadth];

children.text: ardhārdhenāparāḥ śītāḥ śeṣaṃ bāhyo mahodadheḥ // VAkK_3.52 //
children.translated_text: the other cold [lakes diminish] by half-and-half; the rest is the great outer ocean. // VAkK_3.52 //

children.text: lakṣatrayaṃ sahasrāṇi viṃśatirdve ca tatra tu /
children.translated_text: Three hundred and twenty-two thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] — and there,
<s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is two thousand, with three sides, cart-shaped. // VAkK_3.53 //
One [side] is three and a half <s>yojanas</s>; <s>Pūrvavideha</s> is half-moon shaped;

children.text: pārśvatrayaṃ tathāsya ekaṃ sārdhaṃ triśatayojanam // VAkK_3.54 //
children.translated_text: its three sides are likewise, and one is three hundred and fifty <s>yojanas</s>. // VAkK_3.54 //
<s>Godānīya</s> is seven and a half thousand, circular;

children.text: sārdhe dve madhyamasya aṣṭau caturasraḥ kuruḥ samaḥ // VAkK_3.55 //
children.translated_text: two and a half [thousand] is the middle; <s>Uttarakuru</s> is eight [thousand], square, and equal. // VAkK_3.55 //
<s>Deha</s>, <s>Videha</s>, <s>Kurava</s>, <s>Kaurava</s>, <s>Camara</s>, and <s>Avara</s>,
are the eight sub-continents of those; <s>Gāthā</s> and <s>Uttaramantrin</s>. // VAkK_3.56 //
North of here [<s>Jambūdvīpa</s>], the <s>Kīṭa</s> mountain [range], nine [<s>yojanas</s>]; beyond that, <s>Himavat</s>;
fifty [<s>yojanas</s>] in width and length — a lake, this side of <s>Gandhamādana</s>. // VAkK_3.57 //
Below, by twenty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>], <s>Avīci</s> [hell] has that measure;

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ sapta narakāḥ sarve 'ṣṭau ṣoḍaśotsadāḥ // VAkK_3.58 //
children.translated_text: above that are seven <s>narakas</s> (hells) — all eight have sixteen adjunct [hells]. // VAkK_3.58 //
<s>Kukūla</s> (hot ashes), <s>kuṇapa</s> (corpse-swamp), then <s>kṣuramārga</s> (razor-path) and the rest, and a river —
these [are] in the four directions of those [hells]; the other eight cold [hells begin with] <s>Arbuda</s> and so forth. // VAkK_3.59 //
At half [the height] of <s>Meru</s>, the moon and sun [revolve], fifty-one <s>yojanas</s> [in diameter];
midnight is the setting; midday is the rising, once [per revolution]. // VAkK_3.60 //
In the second month of the rainy season, on the last ninth [day], the night increases;

children.text: hemantānāṃ caturthe tu hīyate aharviparyayāt // VAkK_3.61 //
children.translated_text: in the fourth month of winter, it decreases — the day being the reverse. // VAkK_3.61 //
The increase of night and day [occurs] by portions, when the sun moves southward and northward;
observation of the waning moon is due to its own shadow and proximity to the sun. // VAkK_3.62 //
Its [<s>Meru</s>'s] four terraces are at intervals of ten thousand [<s>yojanas</s>];

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau sahasrāṇi catvāri dve ca nirgatāḥ // VAkK_3.63 //
children.translated_text: sixteen, eight, four, and two thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] they extend outward. // VAkK_3.63 //
On those [terraces dwell] the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s>, <s>Mālādhāra</s>, and <s>Sadāmada</s>,
and the <s>Mahārājika</s> gods; also on the seven mountains. // VAkK_3.64 //
On the summit of <s>Meru</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) [gods]; it [the summit] is eighty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] in each direction;
at the corners, four peaks, inhabited by <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> guardians. // VAkK_3.65 //
In the middle, two and a half thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] on each side, one and a half <s>yojanas</s> [in height],

children.text: puraṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma haimaṃ citratalaṃ mṛdu // VAkK_3.66 //
children.translated_text: is a city named <s>Sudarśana</s>, golden, with variegated pavement, soft. // VAkK_3.66 //
Therein, <s>Vaijayanta</s> [palace] is two hundred and fifty [<s>yojanas</s>] on each side; outside, moreover,
it is adorned with <s>Caitraratha</s>, <s>Pāruṣya</s>, <s>Miśra</s>, and <s>Nandana</s> [groves]. // VAkK_3.67 //
Twenty [<s>yojanas</s>] apart, with beautiful grounds in the four directions of those;
to the northeast, the <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree]; to the southwest, <s>Sudharmā</s> [assembly hall]. // VAkK_3.68 //

children.text: tata ūrdhva vimāneṣu devāḥ kāmabhujastu ṣaṭ /
children.translated_text: Above that, the gods [dwell] in aerial palaces; the desire-realm gods are six [classes];
their sexual union is by copulation, embracing, hand-holding, smiling, gazing, and glancing. // VAkK_3.69 //
A child [matures] from five years in appearance up to ten years in appearance;
beings arise among them fully formed and wearing garments. // VAkK_3.70 //
Three are <s>kāmopapatti</s> (desire-realm rebirths); the desire-gods are the same as humans [in some respects];
three are <s>sukhopapatti</s> (happy rebirths) — nine levels of the three <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations). // VAkK_3.71 //
From a given station, they see downward as far [as they can], and upward from here and there;
they have no upward vision of those [above], except through <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) or dependence on another. // VAkK_3.72 //
The four continents, moon, sun, <s>Meru</s>, the desire-realm celestials,
and a thousand <s>Brahma</s>-worlds — this is considered a 'first-order thousandfold' [world-system]. // VAkK_3.73 //
A thousand of those is a 'second-order' world-system, the middle [thousandfold];
a thousand of those is the 'third-order' [world-system, the great trichiliocosm] — it undergoes simultaneous destruction and formation. // VAkK_3.74 //
The beings of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> measure three and a half cubits in height;
those of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, <s>Godānīya</s>, and <s>Uttarakuru</s> increase by double successively. // VAkK_3.75 //
With quarter-[cubit] increments, the body [grows] thin up to half a <s>krośa</s> for the gods;

children.text: kāmināṃ rūpiṇāṃ tvādau yojanārdhaṃ tataḥ param // VAkK_3.76 //
children.translated_text: for the desire-realm gods, half a <s>yojana</s> at first; then above that, // VAkK_3.76 //
with half-by-half increase upward from [the gods of] <s>Parīttābha</s>, as to the support [body];
doubled and doubled, except from <s>Anabhraka</s>, [increasing by] three <s>yojanas</s>. // VAkK_3.77 //
In <s>Uttarakuru</s>, lifespan is a thousand [years]; for the two [<s>Pūrvavideha</s> and <s>Godānīya</s>], diminished by half and half;

children.text: ihāniyatam ante tu daśābdāḥ ādito 'mitam // VAkK_3.78 //
children.translated_text: here [in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>] it is indefinite; at the end, ten years; at the beginning, immeasurable. // VAkK_3.78 //
Fifty human years equal one day-and-night of the lowest desire-realm gods;
by that reckoning, their lifespan is five hundred years. // VAkK_3.79 //
For those above, both [the day-and-night and lifespan] are doubled successively; but for form-realm beings,
there is no day-and-night — their lifespan is reckoned in <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) equal to their [respective] supports. // VAkK_3.80 //
In the formless realm, twenty thousand <s>kalpas</s>, increasing successively;
a great <s>kalpa</s> [is reckoned] beginning from <s>Parīttābha</s>; below that, below <s>Adharma</s>, then — // VAkK_3.81 //
the day-and-night in the [hells] is equal to the lifespan of the desire-gods, in order;
the lifespan in <s>Saṃjīva</s> and the [next] six [hells] is by those [reckonings], like the desire-gods. // VAkK_3.82 //
Half [a great <s>kalpa</s>] in <s>Pratāpana</s>; in <s>Avīci</s>, an intermediate <s>kalpa</s>; and the highest, moreover,

children.text: kalpaṃ tiraścāṃ pretānāṃ māsānhā śatapañcakam // VAkK_3.83 //
children.translated_text: a [full] <s>kalpa</s>; for animals and <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), their maximum [lifespan] is five hundred months. // VAkK_3.83 //
From a <s>vāha</s>-vessel, [removing] one sesame seed per hundred years — [when it is] exhausted, such is the lifespan [of the <s>Arbuda</s> hell];
the others from <s>Arbuda</s> have lifespans increasing by twenty-fold successively. // VAkK_3.84 //
Outside <s>Uttarakuru</s>, there is untimely death. <s>Paramāṇu</s> (atom), <s>akṣara</s> (syllable), and <s>kṣaṇa</s> (instant) —
these are the limits of <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>nāma</s> (name), and <s>adhvan</s> (time). The <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), the <s>aṇu</s> (minute particle), likewise — // VAkK_3.85 //
iron, water, rabbit-hair, a gap of sunlight, a mote, a nit, a louse — those produced from them,
a barley-grain, then a finger-joint — each should be known as seven times [the previous]. // VAkK_3.86 //
Twenty-four finger-widths make a cubit; four cubits make a <s>dhanus</s> (bow-length);

children.text: dhanuḥ pañcaśatānyeṣāṃ krośo raṇyaṃ ca tanmatam // VAkK_3.87 //
children.translated_text: five hundred of those make a <s>krośa</s> — and that is also called a <s>raṇya</s>. // VAkK_3.87 //
Eight of those, they say, make a <s>yojana</s>. Again, twenty times one hundred

children.text: tatkṣaṇaḥ te punaḥ ṣaṣṭirlavaḥ triṃśad guṇottarāḥ // VAkK_3.88 //
children.translated_text: make a <s>tatkṣaṇa</s> (moment); sixty of those make a <s>lava</s>; thirty [<s>lavas</s>] increase successively. // VAkK_3.88 //
Three <s>muhūrtas</s> make a day-and-night; twelve months

children.text: saṃvatsaraḥ sonarātraḥ kalpo bahuvidhaḥ smṛtaḥ // VAkK_3.89 //
children.translated_text: make a year, along with intercalary nights; <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) is said to be of many kinds. // VAkK_3.89 //
The <s>saṃvartta-kalpa</s> (dissolution aeon) [extends] from the arising of beings in hell to the destruction of the receptacle [world];
the <s>vivartta-kalpa</s> (formation aeon) [extends] from the prior wind until the arising of beings in hell. // VAkK_3.90 //
An intermediate <s>kalpa</s> [extends] from an immeasurable [lifespan] to a lifespan of ten years; then

children.text: utkarṣā apakarṣāśca kalpā aṣṭā daśāpare // VAkK_3.91 //
children.translated_text: there are increases and decreases — eighteen further <s>kalpas</s>. // VAkK_3.91 //
One increase — those [lifespans extend] from eighty thousand years as the lifespan [upward];

children.text: iti loko vivṛtto 'yaṃ kalpāṃstiṣṭhati viṃśatim // VAkK_3.92 //
children.translated_text: thus, this world, having been formed, endures for twenty <s>kalpas</s>. // VAkK_3.92 //
Then it forms; having been destroyed, it remains [empty]; and it is destroyed — equally;
these [four phases of] eighty [intermediate <s>kalpas</s> constitute] a great <s>kalpa</s>; from three <s>asaṃkhyeyas</s> (incalculable aeons) of those arises — // VAkK_3.93 //
<s>Buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood). In the period of decrease, from one hundred [years lifespan] to that arising;
for the two [types], <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones); the rhinoceros-like [<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>] arises over a hundred <s>kalpas</s>. // VAkK_3.94 //
The arising of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) [does not occur] below an eighty-thousand[-year lifespan];
the <s>Cakravartins</s> of gold, silver, copper, and iron [wheels are ranked] in descending order. // VAkK_3.95 //

children.text: ekadvitricaturdvīpāḥ na ca dvau saha buddhavat /
children.translated_text: [They rule] one, two, three, or four continents; two [<s>Cakravartins</s>] do not [arise] simultaneously, like <s>Buddhas</s>;
they [are distinguished by] coming forth to meet, going of their own accord, contention, and conquest by weapons. // VAkK_3.96 //
By [being] partial, established, heated, and complete, the distinction of marks of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) [is superior];

children.text: prāgāsan rūpivat sattvāḥ rasarāgāttataḥ śanaiḥ // VAkK_3.97 //
children.translated_text: formerly, beings were like form-realm beings; then, due to attachment to taste, gradually — // VAkK_3.97 //
from laziness, having accumulated provisions, a field-protector was hired by the covetous;
then, due to the increase of unwholesome <s>karmapatha</s> (courses of action), when [the lifespan] decreased to ten years — // VAkK_3.98 //
the destruction of the <s>kalpa</s> [occurs] through weapons, disease, and famine;

children.text: divasān sapta māsāṃśca varṣāṇi ca yathākramam // VAkK_3.99 //
children.translated_text: lasting seven days, seven months, and seven years, respectively. // VAkK_3.99 //
The destructions are again threefold, [occurring] by fire, water, and wind;

children.text: dhyānatrayaṃ dvitīyādi śīrṣa tāsāṃ yathākramam // VAkK_3.100 //
children.translated_text: the second, third, and [fourth] <s>dhyānas</s> are the upper limits of those [destructions] respectively. // VAkK_3.100 //
Because of similarity to the absence of that [which is to be purified], the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] is not [destroyed], since it is unshakeable;

children.text: na nityaṃ saha sattvena tadvimānodayavyayāt // VAkK_3.101 //
children.translated_text: it is not permanent together with beings, because of the arising and perishing of their mansions. // VAkK_3.101 //

children.text: saptāgninā adbhirekā evaṃ gate 'dbhiḥ saptake punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seven [destructions] by fire, one by water — when a [cycle of] seven has thus passed, again by water a set of seven;
then a set of seven by fire, and after that a wind-destruction. // VAkK_3.102 //

body.text: abhidharmakośabhāṣye lokanirdeśo nāma tṛtīyaṃ kośasthānam samāptamiti /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośabhāṣya</s>, the third <s>kośasthāna</s> entitled 'Exposition of the World' (<s>Lokanirdeśa</s>) is concluded. /
Whatever merit there is herein belongs to the venerable <s>Lāmāvāka</s>. /

children.text: karmajaṃ lokavaicitryaṃ cetanā tatkṛtaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The diversity of the world is born of <s>karma</s> (action); that [<s>karma</s>] is <s>cetanā</s> (volition) and what is done by it;

children.text: cetanā mānasaṃ karma tajjaṃ vākkāyakarmaṇī // VAkK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is mental <s>karma</s>; what is born from it is vocal and bodily <s>karma</s>. // VAkK_4.1 //
Those [vocal and bodily karmas] are <s>vijñapti</s> (intimation) and <s>avijñapti</s> (non-intimation); <s>kāyavijñapti</s> (bodily intimation) is held to be

children.text: saṃsthānaṃ na gatiryasmātsaṃskṛtaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ vyayāt // VAkK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: a configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), not movement, since whatever is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is momentary, due to destruction. // VAkK_4.2 //

children.text: na kasyacidahetoḥ syāt hetuḥ syācca vināśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nothing could exist without a cause, and a cause would be a destroyer [if it caused destruction];

children.text: dvigrāhyaṃ syāt na cāṇau tat vāgvijñaptistu vāgdhvaniḥ // VAkK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: it would be apprehended by two [senses] — but that is not [the case] for atoms; <s>vāgvijñapti</s> (vocal intimation), however, is vocal sound. // VAkK_4.3 //
It is threefold [as] stainless by the statement of form, increase, non-production-of-the-path, and so forth;
from the moment onward, <s>avijñapti</s> (non-intimation) [arises]; it is obtained in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), past, and born from elements. // VAkK_4.4 //
Bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> that is with <s>āsravas</s> (contaminants) depends on its own elements (<s>bhūtas</s>);
the <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free) [<s>karma</s> depends on elements] where one is born; <s>avijñapti</s> is non-appropriated (<s>anupāttikā</s>). // VAkK_4.5 //
That which is an outflow (<s>naiḥṣyandikī</s>) is called 'of sentient beings,' born from outflow and appropriated elements;
that born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is a product, born from non-appropriated, undifferentiated elements. // VAkK_4.6 //
There is no <s>avijñapti</s> that is indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); otherwise [it is] threefold; the unwholesome, moreover,

[exists] in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm); <s>avijñapti</s> also [exists] in <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm); <s>vijñapti</s> [exists] in the two [realms] with <s>vicāra</s> (discursive thought). // VAkK_4.7 //
In <s>Kāmadhātu</s> also, the restrained [<s>avijñapti</s>] does not exist, since there is no origination from a non-existent;
liberation is ultimately wholesome; from itself [arise] the roots, shame, and modesty. // VAkK_4.8 //
Through association, those conjoined with it [are wholesome]; through origination, actions and so forth [are wholesome];
by the reverse, [<s>karma</s> is] unwholesome; the ultimately indeterminate is fixed. // VAkK_4.9 //
Origination (<s>samutthāna</s>) is twofold, designated as causal and that-moment-arising;
of those two, the first is the impelling [factor], the second is the sustaining [factor]. // VAkK_4.10 //
The impelling [factor] is consciousness abandoned by seeing (<s>darśana</s>); both [impelling and sustaining] moreover
[operate for] the mental; what is abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is fivefold and is only sustaining. // VAkK_4.11 //
For in the impelling [factor] the wholesome and so forth may be threefold, yet the sustaining [factor]

children.text: tulyaṃ muneḥ śubhaṃ yāvat nobhayaṃ tu vipākajam // VAkK_4.12 //
children.translated_text: is equal [to the Sage's] wholesome as long as [it lasts]; but neither is <s>vipākaja</s> (resultant). // VAkK_4.12 //
<s>Avijñapti</s> (non-intimation) should be known as threefold: restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>), and other;
restraint is [of three kinds]: that called <s>prātimokṣa</s>, that born of <s>dhyāna</s>, and likewise the <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free). // VAkK_4.13 //
The <s>prātimokṣa</s> [restraint] is eightfold, but in substance it is fourfold;

children.text: liṅgato nāmasaṃcārāt pṛthak te cāvirodhinaḥ // VAkK_4.14 //
children.translated_text: by gender, name-designation, and separateness, they are non-contradictory. // VAkK_4.14 //
Through the undertaking of abstinence from five, eight, all, and those to be excluded,
[one becomes] a lay-follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), one observing the fast (<s>upavāsastha</s>), a renunciant (<s>śramaṇa</s>), a novice (<s>uddeśa</s>), or a monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>). // VAkK_4.15 //
<s>Śīla</s> (morality) is good conduct; <s>karma</s> (action) is also called restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>);
in the first [sense], it is <s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s>; <s>prātimokṣa</s> is the path of action (<s>kriyāpatha</s>). // VAkK_4.16 //
Those endowed with <s>prātimokṣa</s> are eight; one endowed with that born of <s>dhyāna</s>;
those with the <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free) are Noble beings (<s>ārya</s>); the last two [restraints] follow the mind. // VAkK_4.17 //
In the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary stage) they are called abandonment, and those two are born of the <s>ānantarya-mārga</s> (uninterrupted path);
full knowledge (<s>saṃprajñāna</s>) and mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) are two [more], [namely] the restraints of mind and faculties. // VAkK_4.18 //
One established in <s>prātimokṣa</s> is always, through non-abandonment, endowed with the present
<s>avijñapti</s>; from the first moment onward, [endowed] with the past one. // VAkK_4.19 //
Likewise one established in non-restraint; one possessing <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint [is endowed] always
with the past and unarisen [<s>avijñapti</s>]; but a Noble One in the first [moment] is not [endowed] with the past. // VAkK_4.20 //
Those two [who are] concentrated and on the Noble Path are joined with the present [<s>avijñapti</s>];

children.text: madhyasthasyāsti cedādau madhyayā ūrdhvaṃ dvikālayā // VAkK_4.21 //
children.translated_text: if one in the intermediate state has it at first, [then endowed] with the intermediate, and after that with the two-time [past and present]. // VAkK_4.21 //
One established in non-restraint [is endowed] with the wholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>]; one established in restraint, with the unwholesome;
[one is] endowed with <s>avijñapti</s> as long as the force of faith or defilement [persists]. // VAkK_4.22 //

children.text: vijñaptyā tu punaḥ sarve kurvanto madhyayānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But with <s>vijñapti</s> (intimation), all [persons] when acting are endowed with the present one;
with the past one from the moment onward until abandonment; there is no unarisen [<s>vijñapti</s>]. // VAkK_4.23 //
One is not endowed with both the restrained and unrestrained that are past;

children.text: asaṃvaro duścaritaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ karma tatpathaḥ // VAkK_4.24 //
children.translated_text: non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) is misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>), immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), <s>karma</s>, and the path of that [<s>karma</s>]. // VAkK_4.24 //
One who acts is endowed with <s>vijñapti</s> only; one in the intermediate [state has] weak volition;
one who has abandoned and [whose <s>vijñapti</s>] has not arisen — the <s>avijñapti</s> [belongs to] a Noble person (<s>ārya-pudgala</s>). // VAkK_4.25 //
That born of <s>dhyāna</s> is obtained only on the <s>dhyāna</s> ground; the <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free) [is obtained] on that [ground]
and on the Noble [ground]; <s>prātimokṣa</s> [is obtained] through the communication of another and so forth. // VAkK_4.26 //
The undertaking [of <s>prātimokṣa</s>] is for life; [the fast is] for a day and night; with [proper] intention,
there is no non-restraint for [just] a day and night, since indeed it is not so undertaken. // VAkK_4.27 //
It should be taken in the morning, from another, [by one] standing lower, having recited what was spoken;
the fast (<s>upavāsa</s>) [must be] with all its limbs complete, unadorned, [lasting until] the end of the night. // VAkK_4.28 //
The limbs of morality (<s>śīla</s>), the limb of non-negligence, and the limbs of observance (<s>vrata</s>) are, in order,

children.text: catvāryekaṃ tathā trīṇi smṛtināśo madaśca taiḥ // VAkK_4.29 //
children.translated_text: four, one, and three; by these [are prevented] loss of mindfulness and intoxication. // VAkK_4.29 //
The fast can belong to another [tradition] too; but not the refuge for one who has not gone [for refuge];
from undertaking the status of a lay-follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), the conventional utterance is like that of a monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>). // VAkK_4.30 //
If all are fully restrained, how [can there be] partial-duty ones and so forth?

children.text: tatpalanāt kila proktāḥ mṛdvāditvaṃ yathā manaḥ // VAkK_4.31 //
children.translated_text: They are so called because of protecting that [partial vow]; just as the mind [is called] soft and so on. // VAkK_4.31 //
He who takes refuge in the threefold refuge: the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>-related <s>dharmas</s>, the beyond-training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), both-sided,

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ ceti śaraṇaṃ yo yāti śaraṇatrayam // VAkK_4.32 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — [these constitute] the refuge. // VAkK_4.32 //
Because sexual misconduct is extremely blameworthy, because of ease, because of non-action being attained,

children.text: yathābhyupagamaṃ lābhaḥ saṃvarasya na saṃtate // VAkK_4.33 //
children.translated_text: the obtaining of restraint is according to one's undertaking, not in the [entire] continuum. // VAkK_4.33 //
And because of the entailment of false speech when transgressing all precepts,
because of the faultiness of rejection — from intoxicants alone, for the sake of guarding [the other precepts]. // VAkK_4.34 //
From all and both [types of] beings obtained in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), [restraint] is obtained from present [beings];
from the fundamental [defilements], from all times — [such are] the <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>anāsrava</s> restraints. // VAkK_4.35 //
Restraint [is taken] from all beings; but there is debate regarding the limbs and causes;

children.text: asaṃvarastu sarvebhyaḥ sarvāṅgebhyo na kāraṇaiḥ // VAkK_4.36 //
children.translated_text: non-restraint, however, [is obtained] from all [beings], from all limbs, not from causes. // VAkK_4.36 //
Non-restraint is obtained by action or by undertaking;
but the obtaining of the remaining <s>avijñapti</s> is through field, gift, respect, and so forth. // VAkK_4.37 //
The abandonment of <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint [occurs] through renunciation of the training, death,
the arising of both sexual characteristics, cutting the root [of virtue], and the passing of the night. // VAkK_4.38 //
And by a <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense, say some; the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, say others;
but the <s>Kāśmīras</s> hold that for one who has fallen, there are two [remaining], like a debt. // VAkK_4.39 //
The wholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>] obtained through <s>dhyāna</s> is lost by change of ground, wandering, and loss;
likewise that obtained in the formless [realm]; but the Noble [<s>avijñapti</s> is lost] by attainment of the fruit, the highest point, and loss. // VAkK_4.40 //
Non-restraint [is lost] by obtaining restraint, death, and the arising of both [sexual] characteristics;
the intermediate [<s>avijñapti</s> is lost] by the cessation of force, gift, action, purpose, lifespan, and cutting the root. // VAkK_4.41 //
The wholesome formless [<s>avijñapti</s>] obtained in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> [is lost] by cutting the root and birth in a higher [realm];
the defiled [<s>avijñapti</s>] is destroyed by the arising of its antidote; but the formless [defiled one] deteriorates. // VAkK_4.42 //
Non-restraint [exists] among humans, excluding <s>śaṇḍhas</s> (eunuchs), <s>paṇḍakas</s> (sexually impotent), those of dual form, and <s>Kurus</s>;

children.text: kurūṃśca saṃvaro 'pyevaṃ devānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ trayaḥ // VAkK_4.43 //
children.translated_text: restraint likewise [excludes these]; for gods and humans, [there are] three [types of restraint]. // VAkK_4.43 //
For gods of <s>Kāmadhātu</s> and <s>Rūpadhātu</s>, [there is] the <s>dhyāna</s>-born [restraint]; the <s>anāsrava</s> (outflow-free), moreover,
[belongs] also to formless beings, excluding those of the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> and the unconscious beings (<s>asaṃjñi-sattvas</s>). // VAkK_4.44 //
<s>Karma</s> (action) is secure, insecure, or neither — [corresponding to] wholesome, unwholesome, and neither;

children.text: puṇyāpuṇyamaniñjaṃ ca sukhevedyādi ca trayam // VAkK_4.45 //
children.translated_text: merit (<s>puṇya</s>), demerit (<s>apuṇya</s>), and the imperturbable (<s>āniñjya</s>); and [that] to be experienced as pleasure and so on — threefold. // VAkK_4.45 //
Wholesome <s>karma</s> in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) is merit (<s>puṇya</s>); <s>āniñjya</s> (imperturbable) is that born above;

children.text: tadbhūmiṣu yataḥ karmavipākaṃ prati neñjati // VAkK_4.46 //
children.translated_text: because in those [higher] grounds, <s>karma</s> does not waver with respect to its fruition. // VAkK_4.46 //
Wholesome [<s>karma</s>] from the first up to the third <s>dhyāna</s> is to be experienced as pleasure; beyond that,
as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure; unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] here [in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>] is to be experienced as suffering. // VAkK_4.47 //
Some [say that] below also there is an intermediate [feeling]; because of the fruition in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>,
since the fruition of the three is held to be neither the first nor the last. // VAkK_4.48 //
By intrinsic nature, association, object, and fruition,
and by confrontation — thus fivefold is the [manner of] being experienced as feeling. // VAkK_4.49 //
That [<s>karma</s>] is determinate and indeterminate; the determinate is again threefold,
due to being experienced in this life and so on; some [hold] <s>karma</s> to be fivefold. // VAkK_4.50 //
Others [say] there is a fourfold alternative (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>); projection into a [birth-]class is by three [karmas];

children.text: sarvatra caturākṣepaḥ śubhasya narake tridhā // VAkK_4.51 //
children.translated_text: projection into all [classes] is fourfold; the wholesome in hell is threefold. // VAkK_4.51 //
One who is detached, stable, or foolish does not produce [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced there;
nor does even a Noble One produce [<s>karma</s>] with a different [type of] experience; nor [one] unstable in the desire realm or above. // VAkK_4.52 //
In <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) projects twenty-two kinds;

children.text: dṛṣṭadharmaphalaṃ tacca nikāyo hyeka eva saḥ // VAkK_4.53 //
children.translated_text: and that [<s>karma</s>] bears fruit in the present life, for that birth-class is indeed just one. // VAkK_4.53 //
That which is done with intense defilement or faith, continuously,

children.text: guṇakṣetre ca niyataṃ tatpitrorghātakaṃ ca yat // VAkK_4.54 //
children.translated_text: and in a field of merit — that is determinate (<s>niyata</s>); and also that which is the murder of parents. // VAkK_4.54 //
<s>Karma</s> whose fruit [is experienced] in this very life is due to the distinction of field and intention;

children.text: tadbhūmyatyantavairāgyāt vipāke niyataṃ hi yat // VAkK_4.55 //
children.translated_text: that which is determinate as to its fruition [is so] due to complete detachment from that ground. // VAkK_4.55 //
Those who have arisen from <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), <s>āraṇā</s> (non-contention), <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), seeing, or <s>arhat</s>-fruit —
the fruit of benefit or harm toward them is experienced immediately. // VAkK_4.56 //
The feeling of wholesome <s>karma</s> without <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) is considered
to be only mental fruition (<s>caitasikī</s>); but [the fruition] of the unwholesome is only bodily (<s>kāyikī</s>). // VAkK_4.57 //
Distraction of mind is [a condition] of mind upon mind; and that is born from <s>karma</s>-fruition,
and from fear, affliction, imbalance, and grief — for those not in <s>Kuru</s> [continent], in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. // VAkK_4.58 //
The statement of crookedness, fault, and <s>kaṣāya</s> (defilement) [refers to] deceit and [<s>karma</s>] born of hatred and passion respectively;
