furthermore, <s>karma</s> is fourfold by the division of black, white, and so forth. // VAkK_4.59 //
The unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] obtained in <s>Rūpadhātu</s> and <s>Kāmadhātu</s>, and the wholesome [<s>karma</s>], respectively [are]
black and white and both; for the destruction of those, [there is] the outflow-free (<s>nirāsrava</s>) [<s>karma</s>]. // VAkK_4.60 //
In the <s>dharmakṣāntis</s> (patience regarding dharmas), in detachment, and in the eight uninterrupted paths —

children.text: yā cetanā dvādaśadhā karma kṛṣṇakṣayāya tat // VAkK_4.61 //
children.translated_text: whatever <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is twelvefold, that is the <s>karma</s> for the destruction of the black. // VAkK_4.61 //

children.text: navame cetanā yā sā kṛṣṇaśuklakṣayāya ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>cetanā</s> (volition) in the ninth [uninterrupted path] is for the destruction of black and white;
and for [the destruction of] the white, [the <s>cetanā</s>] born of the last uninterrupted path in <s>dhyāna</s>-detachment. // VAkK_4.62 //
Others consider [black <s>karma</s>] to be experienced in hell and [the mixed] to be experienced elsewhere in <s>Kāmadhātu</s>;

children.text: dṛgdheyaṃ kṛṣṇamanye anyatkṛṣṇaśuklaṃ tu kāmajam // VAkK_4.63 //
children.translated_text: some [say] that abandoned by seeing (<s>dṛgheya</s>) is black; others [say] the rest — but that born in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> is black-and-white. // VAkK_4.63 //
The beyond-training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) bodily, vocal, and mental <s>karma</s> respectively

children.text: maunatrayam tridhā śaucaṃ sarva sucaritatrayam // VAkK_4.64 //
children.translated_text: is the threefold silence (<s>mauna</s>); threefold purity (<s>śauca</s>); all good conduct (<s>sucarita</s>) is threefold. // VAkK_4.64 //
The unwholesome bodily <s>karma</s> and the rest is considered to be the threefold misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>);
even what is not [bodily or vocal] <s>karma</s> — covetousness and the rest — is threefold mental misconduct. // VAkK_4.65 //
Good conduct is the reverse [of misconduct]; because of the inclusion of the gross [forms],

children.text: daśa karmapathā uktā yathāyogaṃ śubhāśubhāḥ // VAkK_4.66 //
children.translated_text: ten paths of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmapathāḥ</s>) are taught, wholesome and unwholesome as appropriate. // VAkK_4.66 //
Of the unwholesome [paths], six are <s>avijñapti</s> (non-intimation); one is twofold; these also, for one who is acting,

children.text: dvividhāḥ sapta kuśalāḥ avijñaptiḥ samādhijāḥ // VAkK_4.67 //
children.translated_text: are twofold; the seven wholesome [paths] are <s>avijñapti</s> born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). // VAkK_4.67 //
But in the <s>sāmantakas</s> (preliminary stages), <s>vijñapti</s> (intimation) [may be a path]; <s>avijñapti</s> may or may not exist;
conversely for the subsequent [stages]; the preparatory [stage], however, is born from three roots. // VAkK_4.68 //
Because of arising immediately after that, covetousness and the rest are born from three roots;
the wholesome [paths] ending with the preparatory [stage] are born from non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion. // VAkK_4.69 //
Killing, malice, and harsh speech are completed by hatred; from greed [arise]
adultery, covetousness, and the completion of taking what is not given. // VAkK_4.70 //
Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), however, [is completed] by delusion; for the rest, [completion] by three [roots] is accepted;

children.text: sattvabhogāvadhiṣṭhānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ca nāma ca // VAkK_4.71 //
children.translated_text: the basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) is sentient beings, possessions, and name-and-form, and name [alone]. // VAkK_4.71 //

children.text: samaṃ prāk ca mṛtasyāsti na maulaḥ anyāśrayodayāt /
children.translated_text: Equally, [the path of <s>karma</s>] exists for one who has died before and [for one who dies] simultaneously; the fundamental [path] does not [exist after death], due to the arising of another support.
In armies and such, because of acting as a single unit, all are implicated just as the perpetrator,
<s>Prāṇātipāta</s> (taking life) is the intentional killing of another being without error.
<s>Adattādāna</s> (taking what is not given) is appropriating another's property by force or theft.
Intercourse with a forbidden partner — <s>kāmamithyācāra</s> (sexual misconduct) is fourfold.
Speech that alters the understanding of one who comprehends the meaning, addressed to one of different perception, is <s>mṛṣāvacas</s> (false speech).
What is experienced through the eye, ear, mind, and consciousness, by these three,
is called seen, heard, cognized, and known, respectively, in that order.
<s>Paiśunya</s> (slander) is the speech of one with an afflicted mind aimed at creating division among others.

children.text: pārūṣyamapriyaṃ sarva kliṣṭaṃ bhinna pralāpitā // VAkK_4.76 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pāruṣya</s> (harsh speech) is all that is unpleasant; all that is afflicted is <s>bhinnapralāpitā</s> (idle chatter).
Others say that idle chatter is any other afflicted speech, such as singing, dancing, and prattling;
and also unwholesome speech of that kind. <s>Abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) is wrongful desire for another's property.
<s>Vyāpāda</s> (malice) is hatred toward beings. <s>Nāstidṛṣṭi</s> (nihilistic view) regarding the wholesome and unwholesome

children.text: mithyādṛṣṭiḥ trayo hyatra panthānaḥ sapta karma ca // VAkK_4.78 //
children.translated_text: is <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view). Here there are three paths and seven actions.
The cutting of the root is by wrong view; for those who have obtained rebirth in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm),
by a view that denies both fruit and cause, in all cases progressively, among humans.
A woman cuts it, a man cuts it — one of view-conduct; that is disconnection.
Reconnection is through doubt and belief in existence. One who has committed an <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous act) does not have this.
Simultaneously, one can possess up to eight unwholesome [karma paths],
<s>cetanā</s> (volition) up to ten; but wholesome ones are not [simultaneously] one, eight, or five.
Idle chatter, harsh speech, and malice are twofold in the <s>naraka</s> (hell) realms;
through possession, covetousness and wrong view — in <s>Kuru</s>, three.
The seventh [path] also exists there by itself; in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), elsewhere, ten unwholesome ones.
But three wholesome ones exist everywhere, obtained through direct encounter.
In the formless realm and among unconscious beings, seven are obtained through acquisition;
and also through direct encounter, excluding hell beings and those in <s>Kuru</s>.
All are considered to give results as <s>adhipati</s> (dominant), <s>niṣyanda</s> (outflow), and <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) fruits.
From suffering, death, and destruction of vitality — the fruit is threefold.
Bodily and verbal action born of greed — <s>mithyājīva</s> (wrong livelihood) is distinguished separately,

children.text: duḥśodhatvāt pariṣkāralobhotthaṃ cet na sūtrataḥ // VAkK_4.86 //
children.translated_text: because it is difficult to purify. If one says it arises from greed for requisites, that does not accord with the <s>sūtra</s>.
On the path of abandonment, when with defilements, action bears fruit through five [causes];
through four when without defilements; and other action that is with outflows, whether wholesome or unwholesome,

children.text: anāsravaṃ punaḥ śeṣaṃ tribhiravyākṛtaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: while the remainder that is without outflows — through three; and that which is undesignated,

children.text: catvāri dve tathā trīṇi kuśalasya śubhādayaḥ // VAkK_4.88 //
children.translated_text: four, two, and three respectively are the wholesome and other [fruits] of wholesome [action].
For unwholesome action, the wholesome-beginning [fruits] are two, three, and four in sequence;

children.text: avyākṛtasya dve trīṇi trīṇī caite śubhādayaḥ // VAkK_4.89 //
children.translated_text: for the undesignated, two, three, and three — these are the wholesome-beginning [fruits].
For all past [action], four; for the middle [present], also future ones;

children.text: madhyamā dve ajātasya phalāni trīṇyanāgatāḥ // VAkK_4.90 //
children.translated_text: for the middle, two; for the unborn, the fruits are three — future ones.
Dharmas of one's own level [give] four; those of another level, three or two.

children.text: śaikṣasya trīṇi śaikṣādyāḥ aśaikṣasya tu karmaṇaḥ // VAkK_4.91 //
children.translated_text: For a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner), three — the learner and so forth; but for an <s>aśaikṣa</s> (adept)'s action,

children.text: dharmāḥ śaikṣādikā ekaṃ phalaṃ trīṇyapi ca dvayam /
children.translated_text: the dharmas beginning with learner and so forth give one fruit, three, and also two.

children.text: tābhyāmanyasya śaikṣādyā dve dve pañca phalāni ca // VAkK_4.92 //
children.translated_text: For one other than those two, the learner and so forth give two, two, five fruits, and also

children.text: trīṇi catvāri caikaṃ ca dṛggheyasya tadādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: three, four, and one — for what is to be abandoned by seeing, those and so forth;

children.text: te dve catvāryatha trīṇi bhāvanāheyakarmaṇaḥ // VAkK_4.93 //
children.translated_text: those are two, four, and then three for action to be abandoned by cultivation.

children.text: apraheyasya te tvekaṃ dve catvāri yathākramam /
children.translated_text: For what is not to be abandoned, those are one, two, and four, respectively.

children.text: ayogavihitaṃ kliṣṭaṃ vidhibhraṣṭaṃ ca kecana // VAkK_4.94 //
children.translated_text: Some say that what is performed without proper method is afflicted, and also what deviates from the rules.
A single [action] projects a single birth; multiple ones bring it to completion.

children.text: nākṣepike samāpattī acitte prāptayo na ca // VAkK_4.95 //
children.translated_text: The [two formless] attainments do not project; nor do acquisitions in a mindless state.
<s>Ānantarya</s> (heinous) actions — [committed] with intense <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), then bad rebirth,
birth in <s>Kuru</s> or as an unconscious being — these are considered the three obstructions.

children.text: triṣu dvipeṣvānantarya śaṇḍhā dīnāṃ tu neṣyate /
children.translated_text: In three continents, <s>ānantarya</s> acts [are possible]; but for <s>ṣaṇḍha</s> (eunuchs) and the wretched, they are not accepted,
because of their small capacity for benefit and lack of shame; in the remaining five destinies likewise.
<s>Saṃghabheda</s> (schism of the community) is not a real entity in its own nature; it is dissociated [from mind],
an unafflicted, undesignated <s>dharma</s>. The <s>saṃgha</s> is endowed with it.
The offense in that is false speech; the schism-maker is endowed with it.

children.text: avīcau pacyate kalpam adhikairadhikā rujaḥ // VAkK_4.99 //
children.translated_text: He is tormented in <s>Avīci</s> for a <s>kalpa</s> (eon); with additional [offenses], the suffering increases.

children.text: bhikṣurdṛk carito vṛttī bhinatti anyatra bāliśān /
children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), one of view-conduct, with livelihood — splits [the saṃgha]; except the foolish.
When the Teacher is present, and when there is another path, and when there is patience — the split one does not dwell [in schism].

children.text: cakrabhedaḥ sa ca mataḥ jambūdvīpe navādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That is considered a wheel-schism, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> only, with nine or more [monks].
Action-schism occurs in three continents, with eight or more.
At the beginning, at the end, before the first <s>arbuda</s> [period], after the cessation of a [world] age, and when the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) has passed away,

children.text: sīmāyāṃ cāpyabaddhāyāṃ cakrabhedo na jāyate // VAkK_4.102 //
children.translated_text: and also in an unbound territory — a wheel-schism does not arise.
Because of the destruction of benefit, qualities, and the field, and because of rejection,
even one separated by a sex change may [commit ānantarya] — as a mother, from whom one was born from blood.
For one who strikes a <s>Buddha</s> without the intention to kill, from the blow onward, he does not become an <s>arhat</s>.
For one engaged in <s>ānantarya</s> action, the attainment of the fruit of dispassion is impossible.
False speech in <s>saṃghabheda</s> (splitting the community) is considered the most blameworthy of all.
The volition of <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence) is the most fruitful wholesome [action] in the world.
Corrupting [a nun who is] a mother, [killing] an <s>arhat</s>, killing one who is in the fixed [state of certainty],
killing a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner), or stealing what belongs to the <s>saṃgha</s>.
These are similar to <s>ānantarya</s> acts — the fifth is destroying a <s>stūpa</s>.
They greatly obstruct the attainment of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), the state of a non-returner, and <s>arhatship</s>.

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ kuto yāvat yato lakṣaṇa karmakṛt /
children.translated_text: From where does the <s>bodhisattva</s> [begin], and up to when? From when he performs the <s>lakṣaṇa</s>-creating actions.
He is of good rebirth, noble family, with complete faculties, male, remembering past lives, and irreversible.
In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, as a male only, directly before a <s>Buddha</s>, with volition,

children.text: cintāmayaṃ kalpaśate śeṣa ākṣipate hi tat // VAkK_4.109 //
children.translated_text: born of reflection — over a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (eons), the remainder projects that [result].
Each [mark] is born from a hundred [acts of] merit; [the bodhisattva path lasts] three incalculable [eons] at whose ends,
<s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, and formerly <s>Śākyamuni</s> [appeared].
The perfection of <s>dāna</s> (giving) is giving everything to everyone, out of compassion;
even when limbs are cut, without anger — for one still with attachment — [this completes] <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>śīla</s> (morality).
Through the hymn to [the Buddha] <s>Tiṣya</s>, [the perfection of] <s>vīrya</s> (effort); of <s>dhī</s> (wisdom) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), immediately after.

children.text: puṇyaṃ kriyātha tadvastu trayaṃ karmapathā yathā // VAkK_4.112 //
children.translated_text: Merit is of action, and its basis is threefold, as are the karma paths.
That by which something is given is <s>dāna</s> (giving), with the desire for worship and benefit;

children.text: kāyavākkarma sotthānaṃ mahābhogyaphalaṃ ca tat // VAkK_4.113 //
children.translated_text: it is bodily and verbal action together with its arising, and its fruit is great enjoyment.
One gives for one's own benefit, for the benefit of others, for both, or for neither.
The distinction of that [giving] is further [determined] by the distinction of the donor, the gift, and the field.

children.text: dātā viśiṣṭaḥ śraddhādyaiḥ satkṛtyādi dadāti ataḥ /
children.translated_text: The donor is distinguished by faith and so forth; therefore he gives with respect and so on.
[The distinctions are:] respect, generosity, good intention, timeliness, not depriving [others], and acquisition.
The gift is distinguished by excellence of color and so forth — [giving what produces] beautiful form, fame,
being beloved, having a delicate body, and a body pleasant to touch in all seasons.
The field is distinguished by [the recipient's] rebirth destiny, suffering, helpfulness, and qualities.

children.text: agraṃ muktasya muktāya bodhisattvasya ca aṣṭamam // VAkK_4.117 //
children.translated_text: The highest [gift] is from a liberated one to a liberated one, and to a <s>bodhisattva</s> on the eighth [stage].
Immeasurable is the offering to mothers, fathers, the sick, Dharma-preachers, and to one in the last birth,
and to a <s>bodhisattva</s> — the offering is immeasurable even to non-noble ones.
The basis, the field, the foundation, the effort, the volition, and the intention —
through the weak, middling, and strong degrees of these, action is weak, middling, or strong.
Through [completeness of] volition and fulfillment, through ruthlessness, from the opposite [conditions],
from retinue and from maturation — action is said to be accumulated.
Merit from giving at a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) accrues as in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and so forth — without a recipient.
Even in a bad field, the desired fruit [comes], because the fruit and seed are not reversed.
<s>Dauḥśīlya</s> (immorality) is unwholesome form; <s>śīla</s> (morality) is the abstention from it, which is twofold;

children.text: pratikṣiptācca buddhena viśuddhaṃ tu caturguṇam // VAkK_4.122 //
children.translated_text: and that which is additionally prohibited by the <s>Buddha</s> — the purified [morality] is fourfold.
Free from immorality and its causes, based on the pacification of their opposites,

children.text: samāhitaṃ tu kuśalaṃ bhāvanā cittavāsanāt // VAkK_4.123 //
children.translated_text: the concentrated wholesome [state] — that is <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), from the impression upon the mind.
<s>Śīla</s> (morality) is primarily for heaven; <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation) is for complete liberation.

children.text: caturṇāṃ brāhmapuṇyatvaṃ kalpaṃ svargeṣu modanāt // VAkK_4.124 //
children.translated_text: The four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) have merit [that causes] rejoicing in the heavens for a <s>kalpa</s> (eon).
<s>Dharmadāna</s> (gift of Dharma) is the unafflicted teaching of <s>sūtras</s> and so forth, in accordance with reality.
Wholesome [action] is threefold: conducive to merit, to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and to penetration.
Action set in motion by practice, together with its originator, is threefold:

children.text: lipimudre sagaṇanaṃ kāvyaṃ saṃkhyā yathākramam // VAkK_4.126 //
children.translated_text: writing, seal-making with calculation, poetry, and enumeration, respectively.

children.text: sāvadyā nivṛtā hīnāḥ kliṣṭāḥ dharmāḥ śubhāmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: Blameworthy, obstructed, inferior, afflicted dharmas; wholesome and pure ones;
excellent ones — wholesome conditioned [dharmas] to be cultivated; but <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is unsurpassed.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, the Exposition on <s>Karma</s> (Action).

children.translated_text: The root of existence is the <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions), which are six: <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion),

children.text: māno 'vidyā ca dṛṣṭiśca vicikitsā ca te punaḥ // VAkK_5.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view), and <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt). These, moreover,
are said to be seven through the division of <s>rāga</s> (attachment); <s>bhavarāga</s> (attachment to existence) arises from two realms,
because of being inwardly directed, and to distinguish it from the perception of liberation from that.
The <s>dṛṣṭis</s> (views) are five: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection), <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), <s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view),
<s>dṛṣṭi</s> (speculative view), <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (attachment to rites and rituals) — thus [the anuśayas] become ten.
These ten — seven, seven, eight, minus two or three views respectively —
are abandoned in order by seeing suffering and the other [truths] in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm).
Four are abandoned by cultivation. Those same, but without aversion,
exist in <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) and <s>Ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm) — thus ninety-eight are accepted.
Those arising from <s>bhavāgra</s> (peak of existence) are to be killed by <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and are abandoned by seeing only; the rest
are abandoned by both seeing and cultivation; those not killed by patience are abandoned by cultivation alone.
The six views are: self and mine, permanence and annihilation, nihilism and inferiority,
non-causality and non-path — those are the [respective contents of the] five views.
Regarding <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and others, it operates from the error of a permanent self;
the adherence to [false] causes — therefore that is abandoned only by seeing suffering.
From three views, the four errors arise through inversion:

children.text: nitīraṇāt samāropāt saṃjñācitte tu tadvaśāt // VAkK_5.9 //
children.translated_text: from [wrong] determination and superimposition — [these are errors of] perception and mind, through the influence of those [views].
The <s>mānas</s> (prides) are seven, of nine kinds; from three [roots], they are destroyed by seeing and cultivation.
<s>Vadhādi-paryavasthāna</s> (secondary afflictions beginning with violence) are likewise to be abandoned by cultivation.
The desire for non-existence does not arise in a noble one, nor do prescriptions and the like,

children.text: nāsmitā dṛṣṭipuṣṭatvāt kaukṛtyaṃ nāpi cāśubham // VAkK_5.11 //
children.translated_text: nor the conceit 'I am,' because it is nourished by views; nor unwholesome remorse.
Universal [afflictions] are those abandoned by seeing suffering and the origin [of suffering]: the views,

children.text: vimatiḥ saha tābhiśca yāvidyāveṇikī ca yā // VAkK_5.12 //
children.translated_text: doubt, together with them, and the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) that is specific [to each truth].
Nine have upper-realm objects, among these, excluding two views;
excluding acquisition, those co-arising — whatever [dharmas] are with them, they too are universal.
<s>Mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) and doubt, with the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) connected to them, and also that which is independent —
these are abandoned by seeing cessation and the path; six have <s>anāsrava</s> (uncontaminated) objects.
Cessation of one's own level is the path; [afflictions are] of six levels and nine levels.
The object of those [afflictions] whose object is the path — that path is different, and has a different cause.
There is no <s>rāga</s> (attachment) [toward the path] because it is to be abandoned; no <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) because it does no harm;

children.text: na māno na parāmarśau śāntaśuddhyagrabhāvataḥ // VAkK_5.16 //
children.translated_text: no <s>māna</s> (pride), no <s>parāmarśa</s> (clinging to views) — because of its peacefulness, purity, and supreme nature.
The universal <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions) pervade all [dharmas] entirely,
with respect to their own level and objects; non-universal ones [pervade] their own category.
They do not have uncontaminated or upper [realm] objects, because of non-acceptance and being the opposite.

children.text: yena yaḥ saṃprayuktastu sa tasmin saṃprayogataḥ // VAkK_5.18 //
children.translated_text: Whatever [affliction] is associated with whatever [dharma], that [affliction pervades] it through association.
Above [i.e., in higher realms], all are undesignated; in <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection),

children.text: antagrāhaḥ sahābhyāṃ ca mohaḥ śeṣāstvihāśubhāḥ // VAkK_5.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>antagrāha</s> (extreme view), together with the <s>moha</s> (delusion) associated with them — [these are undesignated]; the rest here are unwholesome.
In the desire realm, the <s>akuśalamūlas</s> (unwholesome roots) are <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>mūḍhi</s> (delusion);
the three <s>akuśalamūlas</s> (unwholesome roots) are <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and that same <s>mati</s> (view). // VAkK_5.20 //
In the two higher [realms], because of the nature of their arising, there are no other two [i.e. aversion is absent]; therefore only four — thus say the outsiders (<s>bāhyakāḥ</s>);

[the unwholesome roots are] <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), [wrong] <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view), <s>māna</s> (pride), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) — they [function] through contemplation by means of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // VAkK_5.21 //
[A question may be answered] categorically in one way, by distinguishing, by counter-questioning,
or by setting aside — [as with questions about] death-and-rebirth, [whether the self is] distinct or identical, and so forth. // VAkK_5.22 //
One may be connected (<s>saṃyukta</s>) with <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>māna</s> (pride) that are past or present —
wherever [a defilement] has arisen and not been abandoned, one is connected with it with respect to that object. // VAkK_5.23 //
Everywhere [one is connected] with these [defilements] that are future, mental, belonging to one's own time-period, and with those of others;

children.text: ajaiḥ sarvatra śeṣaistu sarvaiḥ sarvatra saṃyutaḥ // VAkK_5.24 //
children.translated_text: with those unarisen, everywhere; and with the remaining [defilements], one is connected with all [of them] everywhere. // VAkK_5.24 //
The existence of all [<s>dharmas</s>] in all times is [established] because it has been stated, because of the twofold [argument], because the object exists, because of the fruit,
and because of the assertion 'it exists' — thus the <s>Sarvāstivādins</s> are accepted [as correct]; [their thesis is] fourfold. // VAkK_5.25 //
They are designated as [the theories of] <s>bhāva</s> (essential nature), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characteristic), <s>avasthā</s> (state), and <s>anyathānyathika</s> (mutual difference);

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śobhanaḥ adhvānaḥ kāritreṇa vyavasthitāḥ // VAkK_5.26 //
children.translated_text: the third is excellent; the time-periods (<s>adhvānaḥ</s>) are established by [their] activity (<s>kāritra</s>). // VAkK_5.26 //

children.text: kiṃ vighnaṃ tatkathaṃ nānyat adhvāyogaḥ tathā sataḥ /
children.translated_text: What is the obstacle? How [is it] not otherwise? The application of time-periods to what exists thus —

children.text: ajātanaṣṭatā kena gambhīrā khalu dharmatā // VAkK_5.27 //
children.translated_text: by what [is something] unborn or destroyed? Profound indeed is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. // VAkK_5.27 //
When [defilements] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering have been abandoned, one is [still] connected with the remaining universal [defilements];

children.text: prāk prahīṇe prakare ca śeṣaistadviṣayairmalaiḥ // VAkK_5.28 //
children.translated_text: when those of a preceding category have been abandoned, [one is connected] with the remaining defilements that have that [preceding category's] objects. // VAkK_5.28 //
Those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the cause, and by cultivation, that arise in the desire realm,
have as their domain the defilements of their own three [truths], one [truth of the] form [realm], and consciousness. // VAkK_5.29 //
Those arising in the form realm [have as domain] the defilements of their own [realm], the lower three [truths], and one higher [truth];
those arising in the formless realm [have as domain defilements] of three realms, the three [truths], and the undefiled. // VAkK_5.30 //
Those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation and the path — all have as their domain their own [realm] and the higher;
the undefiled [defilements have as domain] the three realms, the last three [truths], and the undefiled. // VAkK_5.31 //
That which has <s>anuśaya</s> (latent defilement) is twofold: defiled and undefiled — [the latter] by virtue of the latent defilements [adhering to it];
<s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>ākāṅkṣā</s> (doubt), then <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), then <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body), // VAkK_5.32 //
then <s>antagrahaṇa</s> (seizing of extremes), from that <s>śīlāmarśa</s> (attachment to rules and vows), then from that [wrong] view,

children.text: rāgaḥ svadṛṣṭau mānaśca dveṣo 'nyatra ityanukramaḥ // VAkK_5.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>rāga</s> (attachment) toward one's own view, <s>māna</s> (pride), and <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) toward [views] other [than one's own] — this is the sequence. // VAkK_5.33 //
From an <s>anuśaya</s> (latent defilement) that has not been abandoned, from an object that is present,
and from <s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s> (improper mental attention) — [these are] the complete causes of a <s>kleśa</s> (defilement). // VAkK_5.34 //
In the desire realm, the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) with their <s>paryavasthānas</s> (envelopments) are the <s>kāmāsrava</s> (outflow of desire), excluding

children.text: mohena anuśayā eva rūpārūpye bhavāsravaḥ // VAkK_5.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>moha</s> (delusion); as <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements) alone in the form and formless realms, [they constitute] the <s>bhavāsrava</s> (outflow of existence). // VAkK_5.35 //
For those [defilements of the higher realms] are morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) and inwardly directed, belonging to the level of concentration;
therefore they are grouped together; <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the root — hence [it constitutes] a separate <s>āsrava</s> (outflow). // VAkK_5.36 //
Likewise for the <s>oghas</s> (floods) and <s>yogas</s> (bonds); but the separation of [wrong] views is due to their intensity;
[those defilements that are] not in the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows), being without companions — for they are said to have no affinity [with them]. // VAkK_5.37 //
As stated, those same [defilements] with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) [become] twofold through the distinction of [wrong] views;

children.text: upādānāni avidyā tu grāhikā ne ti miśritā // VAkK_5.38 //
children.translated_text: the <s>upādānas</s> (clingings) — but <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), being a grasper, is not [separately listed], since it is mixed [with the others]. // VAkK_5.38 //
These [defilements] are subtle (<s>aṇu</s>) and persistent (<s>anugata</s>), and they cling (<s>anuśerate</s>) in two ways;
and because they bind (<s>anubadhnanti</s>), therefore they are called <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements). // VAkK_5.39 //
They flow (<s>āsravanti</s>), they pervade (<s>āsayanti</s>), they carry away (<s>haranti</s>), they cause adhesion (<s>śleṣayanti</s>),
and they seize (<s>upagṛhṇanti</s>) — these are the etymologies of <s>āsrava</s> (outflow) and the rest. // VAkK_5.40 //
Furthermore, they are declared fivefold by the division into <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters) and the rest;
because of the substance and the attachment to rules being general, the [wrong] views are a different [class of] <s>saṃyojana</s> (fetter). // VAkK_5.41 //
Since [they are] exclusively unwholesome, and since both are independent,
<s>īrṣyā</s> (envy) and <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) are declared among these as a separate pair of <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters). // VAkK_5.42 //
The <s>avarabhāgīya</s> (pertaining to the lower part) [fetters] are fivefold; by two [of them], there is no transcendence of the desire realm;
by three, there is return; the three are [so called] because of grasping at the entrance, root, and [wrong view]; // VAkK_5.43 //
desire not to go [beyond], confusion about the path, and doubt about the path —
these are the obstacles to liberation in [its] progress — hence the threefold teaching. // VAkK_5.44 //
The <s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s> (pertaining to the upper part) [fetters] are likewise fivefold: two [types of] <s>rāga</s> (attachment) — those arising in the form and formless [realms],
<s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), <s>māna</s> (pride), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) — and the threefold bondage is due to [spiritual] maturity. // VAkK_5.45 //
Whatever other defiled mental factors (<s>caitasāḥ</s>) designated as belonging to the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations) —
they are also <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary defilements) derived from the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), but they are not designated as <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) [themselves]. // VAkK_5.46 //
<s>Āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>anapatrapya</s> (lack of moral dread), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness), <s>uddhava</s> (restlessness),
<s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), and <s>middha</s> (drowsiness) — the <s>paryavasthānas</s> (envelopments) are eightfold. // VAkK_5.47 //
<s>Krodha</s> (anger) and <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment) arise from <s>rāga</s> (attachment); <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), and <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) [also];

there is dispute regarding <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment); from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) [arise] <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>middha</s> (drowsiness), and <s>anapatrapya</s> (lack of moral dread). // VAkK_5.48 //
<s>Kaukṛtya</s> (regret) [arises] from <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt); <s>krodha</s> (anger) and <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy) follow from <s>pratigha</s> (aversion);

children.text: anye ca ṣaṭkleśamalāḥ māyā śāṭhyaṃ madastathā // VAkK_5.49 //
children.translated_text: and six others are the <s>kleśamalas</s> (stains of defilement): <s>māyā</s> (deceit), <s>śāṭhya</s> (dissimulation), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), // VAkK_5.49 //
<s>pradāśa</s> (spite), <s>upanāha</s> (enmity), and <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness) — of these, <s>māyā</s> (deceit) and <s>mada</s> (intoxication) arise from <s>rāga</s> (attachment);
<s>upanāha</s> (enmity) and <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness) arise from <s>pratigha</s> (aversion). // VAkK_5.50 //
<s>Pradāśa</s> (spite) [arises] from attachment to rules (<s>dṛṣṭyāmarśa</s>); <s>śāṭhya</s> (dissimulation) arises from [wrong] view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>);

among these, <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>anapatrapya</s> (lack of moral dread), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>middha</s> (drowsiness), and <s>uddhava</s> (restlessness) are each twofold. // VAkK_5.51 //
The others [of those secondary defilements] are to be abandoned by cultivation; they are independent, and likewise [are] stains;
in the desire realm, three are unwholesome in both ways; the rest are morally indeterminate. // VAkK_5.52 //
<s>Māyā</s> (deceit) and <s>śāṭhya</s> (dissimulation) are [found] in the desire realm and the first two <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), because of deceiving <s>Brahmā</s>;
<s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), and <s>mada</s> (intoxication) [exist] in the three realms; the rest arise in the desire realm. // VAkK_5.53 //
Those established together [with defilements] are to be abandoned by seeing; they belong to the level of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness);

children.text: upakleśāḥ svatantrāśca ṣaḍ vijñānāśrayāḥ pare // VAkK_5.54 //
children.translated_text: the <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary defilements) that are independent have the six <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) as their support; the others [do not]. // VAkK_5.54 //

children.text: sukhābhyāṃ saṃprayukto hi rāgaḥ dveṣo viparyayāt /
children.translated_text: For <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is associated with the two pleasures [bodily and mental]; <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) is the opposite;
<s>moha</s> (delusion) [is associated] with all [feelings]; <s>asaddṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) with mental displeasure and mental pleasure; // VAkK_5.55 //
<s>kāṅkṣā</s> (doubt) with <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure); the rest arising in the desire realm with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure);
all also with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity); those belonging to the higher realms [are associated] with their respective [feelings] according to their level. // VAkK_5.56 //
With <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) [are associated] <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness),

children.text: upanāhaḥ pradāśaśca mātsaryaṃ tu viparyayāt // VAkK_5.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>upanāha</s> (enmity), and <s>pradāśa</s> (spite); but <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) is the opposite; // VAkK_5.57 //

children.text: māyā śāṭhyamatho mrakṣo middhaṃ cobhayathā madaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>māyā</s> (deceit), <s>śāṭhya</s> (dissimulation), and <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment) [are associated with mental pleasure]; <s>middha</s> (drowsiness) and <s>mada</s> (intoxication) are twofold [i.e. with both];
[they are associated] with the two pleasures; the universal [envelopments are associated] with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity); the [remaining] four others with five [feelings]. // VAkK_5.58 //
In the desire realm, the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) [are so called] because of [their] function of opposing and nourishing [defilements];
they are twofold [in pairing] and fivefold, because of obstructing the [five] aggregates and [generating] doubt. // VAkK_5.59 //
Through the full knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of the object, through the destruction of that object,
through the abandonment of [grasping] the object, and through the arising of the antidote — [there is] destruction [of defilements]. // VAkK_5.60 //
The antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) is fourfold: as the basis for abandonment, as that which damages,

children.text: pratipakṣaḥ prahātavyaḥ kleśa ālambanāt mataḥ // VAkK_5.61 //
children.translated_text: as the thing to be abandoned, and the <s>kleśa</s> (defilement) [is considered] to be [abandoned] from its object. // VAkK_5.61 //
Due to difference in characteristics, due to being opposed, due to separation in place and time,
the distance of the two is like that of element, character, region, and time-period. // VAkK_5.62 //
[There is] destruction at once; the attainment of <s>visaṃyoga</s> (disconnection) from those [defilements occurs] again and again,
in the arising of the antidote, the attainment of the fruit, and the development of the faculties. // VAkK_5.63 //
The <s>parijñās</s> (full understandings) are nine: the destruction of the two types beginning with the desire realm and so forth;

children.text: ekā dvayoḥ kṣaye dve te tathordhvaṃ tisra eva tāḥ // VAkK_5.64 //
children.translated_text: one [parijñā] at the destruction of two, two at [the destruction of two more] — and above that, three each. // VAkK_5.64 //
The other [parijñās are]: the destruction of the <s>avarabhāgīya</s> (lower fetters), the form [realm fetters], and all <s>āsravas</s> (outflows);

children.text: tisraḥ parijñāḥ ṣaṭ kṣāntiphalaṃ jñānasya śeṣitāḥ // VAkK_5.65 //
children.translated_text: three <s>parijñās</s> (full understandings); six are the fruit of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance); the remaining are [the fruit] of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). // VAkK_5.65 //
All are the fruit of <s>anāgamya</s> (the access absorption); of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), five or alternatively [more];
of the intermediate [absorption], one; and of the basic [absorptions] of the three formless [attainments] as well. // VAkK_5.66 //

children.text: āryamārgasya sarvāḥ dve laukikasya anvayasya ca /
children.translated_text: Of the noble path, all [parijñās result from] two; of the mundane [path] and the <s>anvaya</s> (subsequent [knowledge]) likewise;

children.text: dharmajñānasya tisrastu ṣaṭ tatpakṣasya pañca ca // VAkK_5.67 //
children.translated_text: but of <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the teaching), three; of its counterpart, six; and of the [remaining], five. // VAkK_5.67 //
From the attainment of separation from the undefiled, from the weakening of the peak of existence,
from the uprooting of the twofold cause — <s>parijñā</s> (full understanding) [arises] from the transcendence of realms. // VAkK_5.68 //
One on the path of seeing is endowed with not one [but] up to five [parijñās];

children.text: bhāvanāsthaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍibharekayā vā dvayena vā // VAkK_5.69 //
children.translated_text: one on the path of cultivation, again, with six, with one, or with two. // VAkK_5.69 //
Their accumulation [is determined] from detachment from [each] realm and from the attainment of the fruit;

children.text: ekāṃ dve pañca ṣaṭ kaścijjahātyāpnoti pañca na // VAkK_5.70 //
children.translated_text: someone abandons one, two, five, or six, and obtains five but not [all at once]. // VAkK_5.70 //

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the digression on <s>parijñā</s> (full understanding).
Thus is completed the fifth chapter of the Treasury, called the <s>Anuśayanirdeśa</s> (Exposition on Latent Defilements), in the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>.
Whatever merit [is found] herein belongs to the glorious <s>Lāmāvaka</s>.

children.translated_text: The abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) has been explained [as occurring] through seeing the truths and through cultivation;
the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of cultivation) is twofold; but the one called <s>darśana</s> (seeing) is exclusively undefiled. // VAkK_6.1 //
The truths have been declared to be four: <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination),

children.text: nirodhamārga iti eṣāṃ yathābhisamayaṃ kramaḥ // VAkK_6.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (path) — their order is according to [their] realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>). // VAkK_6.2 //
[All conditioned things are] suffering, because of their connection with the three kinds of <s>duḥkhatā</s> (suffering), in their entirety according to [each] connection;

children.text: manāpā amanāpāśca tadanye caiva sāsravāḥ // VAkK_6.3 //
children.translated_text: pleasant, unpleasant, and those that are neither — all that is with-<s>āsravas</s> (with outflows) [is suffering]. // VAkK_6.3 //

children.text: yatra bhinnena tadbuddhiranyāpohe dhiyā ca tat /
children.translated_text: That where, when broken apart, the cognition of it [ceases] — and that which [disappears] when other [things] are mentally excluded —
is <s>saṃvṛtisat</s> (conventionally real), like a pot or water; <s>paramārthasat</s> (ultimately real) is otherwise. // VAkK_6.4 //
One who has completed [ethical conduct] and possesses <s>śruta</s> (learning) and <s>cintā</s> (reflection) applies himself to <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation);
the cognitions beginning with <s>śrutamayī</s> (born of learning) have name, both [name and object], and object as their domains. // VAkK_6.5 //
Not for one who has the two withdrawals, nor for one [who has] discontent or excessive desire;
<s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is the desire for more when [something] has been obtained; <s>mahecchatā</s> (excessive desire) is desire when [something] has not been obtained. // VAkK_6.6 //
From <s>viparyāsa</s> (perversion), those two are their opposites; they are obtained in the three realms and are undefiled;
<s>alobha</s> (non-attachment) and the <s>āryavaṃśas</s> (noble lineages) — of those, three have contentment as their nature. // VAkK_6.7 //
Activity through the three [types of] action, in opposition to the arising of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) —
for the pacification of desire for possessions, will for activity, [desire for] the present, and [desire for] the ultimate. // VAkK_6.8 //
The entry into that [practice] is through <s>aśubhā</s> (contemplation of impurity) and through <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing),
which are the fetters for those with excessive attachment and excessive discursive thought [respectively], and for all those with attachment. // VAkK_6.9 //
The beginner [practices <s>aśubhā</s>] by expanding and contracting [the visualization] of bones [spread] up to the ocean;
one who has achieved mastery is known from the abandonment of the foot-bone up to half the skull. // VAkK_6.10 //
One who has transcended [ordinary] mental attention [achieves] concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) of the mind between the eyebrows;
<s>alobha</s> (non-attachment) has ten stages; <s>aśubhā</s> (the impure contemplation) has the desire and visible [realms] as its object and arises in humans. // VAkK_6.11 //
<s>Ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing) is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); it has five stages; the breath moves [through the body];

children.text: kāmāśrayā na bāhyānām ṣaḍ vidhā gaṇanādibhiḥ // VAkK_6.12 //
children.translated_text: it has the desire realm as its support, not [that] of external [beings]; it is sixfold through counting and the rest. // VAkK_6.12 //
Because the body [is the basis] of inhalation and exhalation, they are called 'belonging to a living being' and are non-appropriated;

children.text: naiḥṣyandikau nādhareṇa lakṣyete manasā ca tau // VAkK_6.13 //
children.translated_text: they are of the nature of outflow (<s>naiḥṣyandika</s>); not [originating] below; they are observed by the mind. // VAkK_6.13 //
One who has accomplished <s>śamatha</s> (calm) should cultivate the practice of <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness),
through the examination of the two characteristics of body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. // VAkK_6.14 //
<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) born of learning and the rest; the others [are distinguished] by association and object; the order
is according to arising; but the group of four is in opposition to the <s>viparyāsas</s> (perversions). // VAkK_6.15 //
Abiding in the <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>), with a combined object,
one contemplates them as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as non-self. // VAkK_6.16 //
Then arises <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat); that has the four truths as its domain,

children.text: ṣoḍaśākāram ūṣmabhyo mūrdhānaḥ te 'pi tādṛśāḥ // VAkK_6.17 //
children.translated_text: with sixteen aspects; from the heat [stage arise] the <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summits); they too are of the same kind. // VAkK_6.17 //
Both [heat and summit] can decrease, but through <s>dharma</s> [knowledge] and also through the others there is increase;

children.text: tebhyaḥ kṣāntiḥ dvidhā tadvat kṣāntyā dharmeṇa vardhanam // VAkK_6.18 //
children.translated_text: from those [arise] <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance), which is twofold and of the same nature; from <s>kṣānti</s>, increase is through <s>dharma</s> [knowledge]. // VAkK_6.18 //
The supreme [<s>kṣānti</s>] has suffering in the desire realm as its object; it is of the highest degree and lasts one moment;

children.text: tathāgradharmāḥ sarve tu pañcaskandhāḥ vināptibhiḥ // VAkK_6.19 //
children.translated_text: likewise the <s>agradharmāḥ</s> (supreme mundane qualities); but all [of these aids to penetration] are the five aggregates, excluding <s>āpti</s> (acquisition). // VAkK_6.19 //
Thus the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (aids to penetration) are fourfold and born of cultivation;

children.text: anāgamyā ntaradhyānabhūmikam dve tvadho 'pi vā // VAkK_6.20 //
children.translated_text: they belong to the level of <s>anāgamya</s> (access concentration) and the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, but the [first] two may also [belong to] a lower [level]. // VAkK_6.20 //
The <s>agradharmāḥ</s> (supreme qualities) have the desire realm as their support; a woman obtains them as having a twofold support;
a noble one abandons them by abandoning the [corresponding] level; but an ordinary person [loses them only] by death. // VAkK_6.21 //

children.text: ādye dve parihāṇyā ca maulestatraiva satyadṛk /
children.translated_text: The first two [are lost] also by decline; [one attains] from the basic [absorption], seeing the truths therein;
there is fresh attainment in [states] that are deficient; decline is the two [cases of] non-possession. // VAkK_6.22 //
One who has attained the <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit) does not cut the roots [of wholesome dharmas]; one who has attained <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) does not go to the bad destinies;

children.text: śiṣyagotrā nnivartya dve buddhaḥ syāt trīṇyapītaraḥ // VAkK_6.23 //
children.translated_text: one of the disciple lineage, not reverting from two, may become a <s>Buddha</s>; others [may attain] also the three. // VAkK_6.23 //
Until <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), all [merit] in one place; at the end of <s>dhyāna</s>, for the Teacher and the solitary [<s>Buddha</s>] —
prior to those, [there is] the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> (conducive to liberation); liberation swiftly occurs within three births.
That which arises from hearing and reflection — three types of action — is impelled in humans;
from worldly [states], toward the <s>agradharmas</s> (supreme dharmas), <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (patience toward dharma) is undefiled.
Regarding suffering in the desire [realm], then here itself, <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge) [arises]; likewise again,
regarding the remaining suffering, <s>anvayakṣānti</s> (subsequent patience) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) [arise]; similarly for the [remaining] three truths.
Thus this realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) consists of sixteen mind-moments, and is threefold:
called seeing (<s>darśana</s>), object (<s>ālambaka</s>), and function (<s>kārya</s>); it belongs to a single stage, that of the <s>agradharmas</s>.
<s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) [moments] are, respectively, the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) and the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), in sequence;
the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) is for one who has not [yet] seen and [now] sees; therein, fifteen moments [constitute it].
Among those, [practitioners] of dull and sharp faculties are [respectively] the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower) and the <s>dharmānusārin</s> (dharma-follower);
they do not fall back, [have only] <s>bhāvanāheya</s> (to be abandoned by cultivation) [defilements remaining], and are those who have entered the [first] fruit.
Inasmuch as [they are] destroyers of up to five categories [of defilements], at the second [fruit], from the exhaustion of nine [defilements] in the lower [realms],
detached from the desire [realm] or above, they are those who have entered the third [fruit].

children.text: ṣoḍaśe tu phalasthau tau yatra yaḥ pratipannakaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the sixteenth [moment], those two are established in the fruit; wherever one has entered [a fruit],
[they are called] <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> (released through faith) and <s>dṛṣṭyāpta</s> (attained through view), being of dull and sharp faculties respectively.
For one established in a fruit, there is no attainment of a path superior to that fruit; therefore,
one established in a fruit is not one who is striving toward distinction, [but rather] an entrant [to the next fruit].

children.text: navaprakārā doṣā hi bhūmau bhūmau tathā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The defilements in each stage are of nine categories, and likewise the qualities,
through the subdivision of weak, medium, and strong into further weak [medium, and strong divisions].
One established in the [first] fruit whose <s>bhāvanāheya</s> [defilements] are not [yet] exhausted is at most a <s>saptakṛtparama</s> (seven-times-at-most returner);
one who has abandoned three or four [categories of defilements] and has two or three births [remaining] is a <s>kulaṃkula</s> (clan-to-clan).
A destroyer of up to five categories [of defilements] is an entrant to the second [fruit];
one whose sixth category [of defilements] is exhausted is a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner); and that one again,
with the seventh and eighth portions of defilements exhausted, [having] one birth [remaining], is an <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-interval);
and an entrant to the third [fruit] — that one is an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) through the exhaustion of nine [categories of defilements].

That [non-returner] is [classified as]: <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval), <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (upon birth), <s>sasaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (with effort), <s>asaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (without effort),
and <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> (one who streams upward); that one in <s>dhyāna</s> is <s>vyavakīrṇa</s> (intermittent), [or] an <s>akaniṣṭhaga</s> (one who goes to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>).
That one is a <s>pluta</s> (leaper), <s>ardhapluta</s> (half-leaper), <s>sarvacyuta</s> (one who dies from all [heavens]); another goes to <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence);
another goes to the formless [realm], fourfold; yet another attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> here [in this life].
Again, making those threefold by three, nine types of form-realm beings (<s>rūpopaga</s>) are recognized;
their distinction is further [determined] by distinction of <s>karma</s>, <s>kleśa</s> (defilements), and faculties (<s>indriya</s>).
By the classification of the <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>, seven good destinies are recognized;
they [are distinguished] by good and bad conduct or non-conduct, and by having departed [from a realm] or not returned.
A noble one (<s>ārya</s>) whose birth has turned away does not take rebirth in the desire [realm]; one who goes to another realm-level
and rises upward does not partake of sense-faculty transfer or decline.
The fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] is entered beforehand, up to the moment of completion, due to the mixture [of conditions],
for the purpose of rebirth and abiding, and also out of fear of defilements.
Due to the fivefold nature of that [fourth <s>dhyāna</s>], there are five <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) rebirths;
a non-returner who has attained the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) is further considered a <s>kāyasākṣin</s> (bodily witness).
Up to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), one who destroys the eight categories [of defilements] is an entrant to <s>arhatship</s>;
on the uninterrupted path of the ninth [category] as well, that one is [called] <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like).
Through the attainment of the exhaustion of those [defilements], <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of exhaustion) [arises]; that one is then an <s>aśaikṣa</s> (one beyond training), an <s>arhat</s>;

children.text: lokottareṇa vairāgyaṃ bhavāgrāt anyato dvidhā // VAkK_6.45 //
children.translated_text: dispassion from the peak of existence [is attained] by the supramundane [path]; from other [stages], in two ways.
In the case of noble dispassion by the mundane [path], the attainments of disconnection are twofold;
and by the supramundane [path] — some [teachers] say — because of the non-connection of abandoned defilements.
One liberated below the peak of existence possesses the character of having been born above;
dispassion by the undefiled [path] is [attained] through the <s>anāgāmin</s> [path] in all cases.
From a <s>dhyāna</s> or its <s>sāmantaka</s> (preparatory stage), the final liberation path [arises]; for the conquest of three stages,
noble ones do not [use paths] above the <s>sāmantaka</s>; with eight [paths], they conquer their own and higher stages.
The liberation and uninterrupted paths that are mundane [employ], in sequence,
the aspects beginning with 'peaceful' and 'gross' respectively, with higher and lower [stages] as their objects.
If one is unshakeable (<s>akopya</s>), [it is] from <s>kṣayajñāna</s>; [but] the thought of non-arising is not [necessarily so];

children.text: kṣayajñānamaśaikṣo vā dṛṣṭiḥ sarvasya sārhataḥ // VAkK_6.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>kṣayajñāna</s> or the <s>aśaikṣa</s> view — this belongs to all, including the <s>arhat</s>.
The <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (fruits of the ascetic life) is the stainless path; its fruit is both conditioned and unconditioned;
those are eighty-nine [in number]; the liberation paths together with the exhaustions [constitute them].
The establishment of the four fruits is due to the conjunction of five causes:
the prior abandonment [of defilements], the attainment of another path, the exhaustion, and the accumulation, in relation to the fruit.
Then the attainment of the eightfold <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), the cultivation of the sixteen aspects,

children.text: laukikāptaṃ tu miśratvānāsravāptiḥ dhṛteḥ phalam // VAkK_6.53 //
children.translated_text: and what is attained through the mundane [path] — due to its mixed nature, the attainment of the undefiled [is also] a fruit of perseverance.
<s>Brāhmaṇya</s> (the state of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>) and the <s>brahmacakra</s> (Brahmā's wheel) are indeed that [path], because it is the turning of <s>Brahman</s>;
the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma) is the path of seeing, [so called] because of its swift movement and other [qualities], by [the prefix] <s>ara</s> and so forth.

children.text: kāme trayāptiḥ antyasya triṣu nordhva hi dṛkpathaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the desire realm, the attainment of three [fruits is possible]; [but] the last [fruit] is not in the three [lower realms], for the path of seeing does not [arise] above;

children.text: asaṃvegādiha vidhā tatra niṣṭheti cāgamāt // VAkK_6.55 //
children.translated_text: due to the absence of urgency here, there is diversity [of attainment]; therein completion [is possible] — thus says scripture.
Six types of <s>arhats</s> are recognized; five of those arise from <s>śraddhādhimukti</s> (faith-conviction);
their liberation is <s>sāmayikī</s> (temporary); [the sixth] is one of unshakeable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>).
Therefore that one is the <s>asamayavimukta</s> (one liberated not temporarily), and is [called] <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> (one who has attained through view);
some [belong to] that <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) from the beginning; some arrive through strenuous effort (<s>uttāpana</s>).
From the lineage of the four [or] five, there is decline from the fruit, but not from the previous [attainment];

children.text: śaikṣānāryāśca ṣaḍgotrāḥ saṃcāro nāsti darśane // VAkK_6.58 //
children.translated_text: learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and noble ones are of six lineages; there is no transfer [of lineage] in the path of seeing.
Decline should be understood as threefold: from the obtained, from the not-yet-obtained, and from enjoyment;

children.text: antyā śāsturakopyasya madhyā cānyasya tu tridhā // VAkK_6.59 //
children.translated_text: the last [type applies to] the Teacher and the unshakeable one; the middle [type applies to] another, and [they experience it] in three ways.

children.text: mriyate na phalabhraṣṭaḥ tadakārya karoti na /
children.translated_text: One who has fallen from the fruit does not die [in that state]; nor does one perform what would undo the fruit;
on the liberation and uninterrupted paths, nine [levels exist] for the unshakeable one, through repeated cultivation.
In what is attained through view, each one [is] undefiled; among humans there is increase [of faculties];

children.text: aśaikṣo nava niśritya bhūmīḥ śaikṣastu ṣaṭ yataḥ // VAkK_6.61 //
children.translated_text: the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (one beyond training) relies on nine stages, while the <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) on six, since —
having abandoned a fruit endowed with distinction, one attains [another] fruit through enhancement;

children.text: dvau buddhau śrāvakāḥ sapta navaite navadhendriyāḥ // VAkK_6.62 //
children.translated_text: two [types of] <s>Buddhas</s>, seven [types of] <s>śrāvakas</s> — these nine possess the nine dominant faculties.
They are classified by application (<s>prayoga</s>), sensory [capacity], attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), and liberation from both sides;

children.text: pudgalāḥ sapta ṣaṭ tvete dvau dvau mārgatraye yataḥ // VAkK_6.63 //
children.translated_text: the [noble] persons are seven, yet these are six, because [some are counted as] two each in the three paths.
One liberated from both sides is one who has attained <s>nirodha</s> [samāpatti]; the other [is liberated] through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
one who is complete in attainments, faculties, and fruits is called a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>).
The completeness of the <s>aśaikṣa</s> [state comes] from two [sources]; the path, in brief,
is fourfold, called distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), liberation (<s>mukti</s>), uninterrupted (<s>ānantarya</s>), and application (<s>prayoga</s>).
In the <s>dhyānas</s>, the path [of practice is] pleasant; in other stages, painful;
for one of dull understanding, <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) is slow; for the other, <s>abhijñā</s> is swift.
<s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) consists of <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising) and <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of exhaustion); that which is in conformity with it —

children.text: saptatriṃśattu tatpakṣyāḥ nāmato dravyato daśa // VAkK_6.67 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> (factors conducive to awakening) are thirty-seven by name, but ten by substance.

children.text: śraddhā vīryaṃ smṛtiḥ prajñā samādhiḥ prītyupekṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>),
tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and right intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) — wisdom indeed is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness);
vigor is called <s>samyakprahāṇa</s> (right effort); concentrations are the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power);

children.text: pradhānagrahaṇaṃ sarve guṇāḥ prāyogikāstu te // VAkK_6.69 //
children.translated_text: the designation of 'predominant' [applies to all]; all qualities are those belonging to the preparatory [stage].
They are cultivated in the beginner's and <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) stages;

children.text: bhāvane darśane caiva sapta vargā yathākramam // VAkK_6.70 //
children.translated_text: in the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) and in the path of seeing (<s>darśana</s>), the seven groups [are cultivated] in sequence.
The <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) and <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (path-factors) are undefiled; the others are of two kinds [defiled and undefiled];

children.text: sakalāḥ prathame dhyāne anāgamye prītivarjitāḥ // VAkK_6.71 //
children.translated_text: all [factors are] complete in the first <s>dhyāna</s>; in the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation), joy is excluded.
In the second [<s>dhyāna</s>], [all are present] except right intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>); in the two [higher <s>dhyānas</s>], those two [joy and intention] are excluded;

children.text: dhyānāntare ca śīlāṅgaistābhyāṃ ca triṣvarūpiṣu // VAkK_6.72 //
children.translated_text: in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> as well, [factors are present] with the moral conduct factors; and in the three formless [attainments], those two [are excluded].
In the desire realm and at the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), the <s>bodhi</s> and <s>mārga</s> factors are excluded;
in the seeing of three truths, [there is] the attainment of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and confirmed confidence (<s>avyetyaprasāda</s>) in the <s>Dharma</s>;
at the realization of the path (<s>mārgābhisamaya</s>), [there is confirmed confidence] in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> as well;
the <s>Dharma</s> [in which there is confirmed confidence] is the three truths [of suffering, arising, and cessation]; for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: mārgaśca dravyatastu dve śraddhā śīlaṃ ca nirmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: the path as well. By substance, there are [only] two: faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), which are stainless.

children.text: noktā vimuktiḥ śaikṣāṅgaṃ baddhatvāt sā punardvidhā // VAkK_6.75 //
children.translated_text: Liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) is not stated as a learner's factor, because it is [still] bound; moreover, it is twofold:
unconditioned — [namely] the abandonment of defilements; and conditioned — [namely] conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>);

children.text: sāṅgaḥ saiva vimuktī dve jñānaṃ bodhiryathoditā // VAkK_6.76 //
children.translated_text: together with the factors, that same [constitutes] the two liberations; knowledge and <s>bodhi</s> are as previously stated.
The mind of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) that is arising is liberated from obstruction;
but the path that is ceasing abandons that obstruction.
The unconditioned alone is called the <s>dhātu</s> (element); dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is the complete exhaustion of passion (<s>rāga</s>);
the element of abandonment (<s>prahāṇadhātu</s>) is for the others; but <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) refers to [all] things.
One becomes disgusted through the patience and knowledge of suffering and its cause; one becomes dispassionate
through all [knowledges]; one abandons by those [means] — thus the fourfold combination arises.

body.text: abhidharmakośe mārgapudgalanirdeśo nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, the sixth <s>kośasthāna</s> (chapter), called the Exposition of Paths and Persons (<s>Mārgapudgalanirdeśa</s>), is completed.

children.translated_text: The stainless [knowledges] are the <s>kṣāntis</s> (patiences) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of exhaustion) and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising) are not views;

children.text: tadanyobhayathāryā dhīḥ anyā jñānaṃ dṛśaśca ṣaṭ // VAkK_7.1 //
children.translated_text: other [knowledge] that is noble in both ways; other [knowledge that is] <s>jñāna</s>; and the views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) are six.
<s>Jñāna</s> is both defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) and undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>); the first [i.e., defiled] is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>);
the undefiled is twofold: <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge).
Conventional [knowledge] has all things as its object; <s>dharmajñāna</s> has as its domain the suffering and so forth of the desire [realm];
<s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) has as its domain the suffering and so forth of the upper [realms].

children.text: te eva satyabhedena catvāri ete caturvidhe /
children.translated_text: Those same [two], divided according to the [four] truths, are fourfold; these [together with the first two make] four types;
<s>anutpādajñāna</s> and <s>kṣayajñāna</s> are again the first mentioned [i.e., dharmajñāna and anvayajñāna types].
Knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>) arises from the four [knowledges] of suffering and arising, [both] subsequent and dharma;

children.text: bhūmyakṣapudgalotkrāntaṃ naṣṭājātaṃ na vetti tat // VAkK_7.5 //
children.translated_text: it does not cognize what has changed in stage, sense-base, person, or transmigration, nor what has perished or is yet to arise.
That [knowledge of others' minds] belongs to <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s>; the other [knows] another in the moments of seeing;
a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) knows [the minds of those on] three [paths]; a <s>khaḍga</s> (solitary buddha) [knows] three; the <s>Buddha</s> [knows] all, without [need of] application.
<s>Kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of exhaustion) is, with regard to the truths, the ascertainment 'it has been fully known' and so forth;
the thought 'there is nothing more to be fully known' and so forth is considered <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising).
From the standpoint of intrinsic nature and antidote, from [the standpoint of] aspect and object of aspect,
from application, accomplishment, cause, and accumulation — the ten [knowledges are distinguished].
That which is <s>dharmajñāna</s> concerning cessation or the path, on the path of cultivation,
is the antidote to the three realms; [but] for the desire realm, it is not <s>anvayajñāna</s>.
<s>Dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s> have sixteen aspects; conventional [knowledge] is otherwise;

children.text: tathā ca sāṃvṛtaṃ svaiḥ svaiḥ satyākāraiścatuṣṭayam // VAkK_7.10 //
children.translated_text: and likewise, conventional [knowledge] has four sets of aspects, each with its own truth-aspects.
Similarly, knowledge of others' minds — when stainless, and when defiled —
has the aspect of the own-characteristic of its object, and has individual substances as its domain.
The remaining fourteen aspects, excluding emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) and non-self (<s>anātma</s>) [from conventional knowledge] —

children.text: nāmalaḥ ṣoḍaśabhyo 'nya ākāraḥ anye 'sti śāstrataḥ // VAkK_7.12 //
children.translated_text: other than the stainless sixteen, no other aspect exists, according to the treatise.
By substance, the sixteen aspects are [all] wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); each aspect together with that [wisdom]

children.text: ākārayanti sālambāḥ sarvamākāryate tu sat // VAkK_7.13 //
children.translated_text: gives [things their] aspect, [since they are] object-possessing; everything that exists is given an aspect.
The first [conventional knowledge] is of three kinds [wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate]; the others are wholesome; the first [applies] to all stages;

children.text: dharmākhyaṃ ṣaṭsu navasu tvanvayākhyaṃ tathaiva ṣaṭ // VAkK_7.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmajñāna</s> [applies] to six [stages]; <s>anvayajñāna</s> likewise to nine and to six [stages].
Knowledge of others' minds [applies] in the <s>dhyānas</s>; it has the desire and form realms as its basis;
but <s>dharmajñāna</s> has the desire realm as its basis; the other [knowledges] have all three realms as their basis.
One foundation of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) — the <s>dharma</s> [foundation] — [applies to] knowledge of cessation; knowledge of others' minds [has]

children.text: trīṇi catvāri śeṣāṇi dharmadhīgocaro nava // VAkK_7.16 //
children.translated_text: three [foundations]; the remaining [knowledges have] four; the domain of <s>dharmajñāna</s> is nine [things].
Nine [are the domain] of <s>mārgajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s>; for <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> and <s>hetujñāna</s>, two [are the domain];

children.text: caturṇāṃ daśa naikasya yojyā dharmāḥ punardaśa // VAkK_7.17 //
children.translated_text: for the four [remaining knowledges], ten [are the domain]; for no single [knowledge is the domain] not to be connected; and again, ten <s>dharmas</s> [are to be connected];
the <s>dharmas</s> of the three realms, the stainless, and the unconditioned — each twofold in two ways.
The conventional [knowledge] should be understood as one [knowledge] distinct from the others in its own group, due to [its cognizing] non-self. // VAkK_7.18 //
One with passion, endowed with one [type of] knowledge, at the first outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) moment,
at the second [moment], with three; and above that, increasing by one in each of the four [truths]. // VAkK_7.19 //
As they arise, the <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearances) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledges) are cultivated on the path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>);
the future [ones] right there [on that path], and the conventional [knowledge] in the three [sets of] subsequent [knowledges]. // VAkK_7.20 //
Therefore, the one called 'final comprehension' (<s>abhisamayāntya</s>) has the nature of non-arising;
in cessation, the last [knowledge pertains to] one's own and lower grounds, [with] the aspect of one's own truth, [and is] effortful. // VAkK_7.21 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśe ṣaṭ sarāgasya vītarāgasya sapta tu /
children.translated_text: At the sixteenth [moment], six [knowledges] for one with passion, but seven for one free from passion;
on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>) for one with passion, and above that, seven [knowledges] in cultivation. // VAkK_7.22 //
on the <s>ānantarya-mārga</s> (uninterrupted paths) above, and also on the eight liberation paths (<s>mukti-mārga</s>) — // VAkK_7.23 //

body.translated_text: In the cultivation of mastery over the seven grounds, <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), the immovable (<s>akopya</s>) attainment, and the mixed [path],

children.translated_text: for a learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) 'burning off' and liberation, six or seven knowledges are cultivated;
on the uninterrupted path of the six [knowledges], and likewise in the conquest of the <s>Bhavāgra</s> (Peak of Existence) — // VAkK_7.24 //

children.text: navānāṃ tu kṣayajñāne akopyasya daśa bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: nine [knowledges] in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣaya-jñāna</s>); for the immovable one (<s>akopya</s>), ten [knowledges] are cultivated;
in the shifting (<s>saṃcara</s>) of that, and in the final liberation, and in the remaining [cases] as stated, eight [knowledges] are cultivated. // VAkK_7.25 //
The [knowledge] for the sake of dispassion toward which, and the attainment of which — there and below, [it] is cultivated;

children.text: sāsravāśca kṣayajñāne labdhapūrvaṃ na bhāvyate // VAkK_7.26 //
children.translated_text: and the with-<s>āsrava</s> (contaminated) [knowledges] in the knowledge of destruction — what was previously obtained is not cultivated. // VAkK_7.26 //
The cultivation of wholesome conditioned [dharmas] is called 'obtaining' and 'practice';
but the cultivation of what has <s>āsravas</s> (contaminants) is [called] 'counteracting' and 'driving out.' // VAkK_7.27 //
The eighteen exclusive (<s>āveṇika</s>) <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> (qualities unique to a Buddha) are the powers (<s>bala</s>) and so forth:

children.text: sthānāsthāne daśa jñānāni aṣṭau karmaphale nava // VAkK_7.28 //
children.translated_text: regarding what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>), ten knowledges; regarding the fruits of <s>karma</s>, eight; nine; // VAkK_7.28 //
regarding <s>dhyāna</s> (meditations) and the rest, faculties, and <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolute intentions), regarding the realms (<s>dhātu</s>), and regarding the courses of practice —

children.text: daśa vā saṃvṛtijñānaṃ dvayoḥ ṣaṭ daśa vā kṣaye // VAkK_7.29 //
children.translated_text: ten, or conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛti-jñāna</s>) [alone]; regarding two, six; regarding destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>), ten or — // VAkK_7.29 //
regarding previous [lives], moral indifference, passing away, arising, the powers, and <s>dhyāna</s> — the remainder;
in all grounds, by which [knowledge] his power is unobstructed. // VAkK_7.30 //
The body [of a <s>Buddha</s>] has the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; others [say] ten times more at the joints;
the strength of seven [beings] beginning with an elephant — and that [strength] belongs to the tangible sense-field (<s>spraṣṭavyāyatana</s>). // VAkK_7.31 //
The <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessnesses) are fourfold, corresponding to the first and tenth powers;
and to the second and seventh [powers]; three [of the four] have the nature of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). // VAkK_7.32 //
The great compassion (<s>mahā-karuṇā</s>) is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛti-dhī</s>); by [its] requisites, aspects, and objects,
and by [its] equality and supreme [intensity], it differs [from ordinary compassion] in eight ways. // VAkK_7.33 //
Through the accumulations [of merit and knowledge] and the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Body of Dharma), and through beneficial activity for the world,
all <s>Buddhas</s> are equal — not in lifespan, birth, or physical measure. // VAkK_7.34 //
Other qualities are shared with disciples, and some with ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>):
<s>araṇā</s> (non-contentiousness), <s>praṇidhi-jñāna</s> (knowledge of aspiration), <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledges), and other virtues. // VAkK_7.35 //
<s>Araṇā</s> is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛti-jñāna</s>), in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, of one with the immovable (<s>akopya</s>) quality;
[it belongs to] human beings, those in whom [defilements] have not arisen, who have attained the desire [realm], with defilements as its object that have a [real] basis. // VAkK_7.36 //

children.text: tathaiva praṇidhijñānaṃ sarvālambaṃ tu tat tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>praṇidhi-jñāna</s> (aspiration knowledge) — and that [has] all [dharmas] as its object; and similarly,

children.text: dharmārthayorniruktau ca pratibhāne ca saṃvidaḥ // VAkK_7.37 //
children.translated_text: the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) [are fourfold:] regarding <s>dharma</s> (phenomena) and <s>artha</s> (meaning), regarding <s>nirukti</s> (etymological explanation), and regarding <s>pratibhāna</s> (eloquent discourse). // VAkK_7.37 //
The [first] three [have as their object] names, meanings, and speech [respectively], and [the fourth is] unfailing knowledge, in that order;
the fourth is connected with mastery over utterance and the paths [of expression]. // VAkK_7.38 //
That [analytical knowledge of eloquence] has the paths of speech as its object; nine knowledges [apply] on all grounds;

children.text: daśa ṣaḍvārthasaṃvit sā sarvatra anye tu sāṃvṛtam // VAkK_7.39 //
children.translated_text: that analytical knowledge of meaning [involves] ten or six [knowledges] in all [cases]; the others are conventional [knowledge]. // VAkK_7.39 //
In the desire [realm] and the <s>dhyānas</s>, the analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s> [is found]; of speech, in the first [<s>dhyāna</s>] and the desire [realm];
not by means of incomplete ones is that attainment [gained]; these six are at the final limit. // VAkK_7.40 //
That is sixfold, conforming to all grounds;
and that reaches the highest stage of development; for a <s>Buddha</s>, [they are] due to another's effort. // VAkK_7.41 //
<s>Ṛddhi</s> (magical power), divine ear (<s>divya-śrotra</s>), knowledge of others' minds, previous births, death-and-arising, and destruction [of defilements] —

children.text: jñāta sākṣīkriyābhijñā ṣaḍ vidhā muktimārgadhīḥ // VAkK_7.42 //
children.translated_text: the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) are sixfold: 'having known,' 'direct realization,' and the knowledge of the liberation path (<s>mukti-mārga</s>). // VAkK_7.42 //
The [first] four are conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛti-jñāna</s>); knowledge of others' minds comprises five knowledges;

children.text: kṣayābhijñā balaṃ yadvat pañca dhyānacatuṣṭaye // VAkK_7.43 //
children.translated_text: the <s>abhijñā</s> of destruction [of defilements] is a power (<s>bala</s>), like that; five [<s>abhijñās</s>] are in the four <s>dhyānas</s>. // VAkK_7.43 //
They have objects of one's own and lower grounds; they are obtainable through dispassion, but the accustomed ones —
the third [<s>abhijñā</s>] has three [kinds of] <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness); the first [is based on] the ear, <s>ṛddhi</s> on the eye. // VAkK_7.44 //
The <s>abhijñās</s> of divine ear and eye are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); the others are wholesome;

children.text: tisro vidyāḥ avidyāyāḥ pūrvāntādau nivarttanāt // VAkK_7.45 //
children.translated_text: three are [called] <s>vidyā</s> (true knowledges), because they counteract <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) regarding the past and so forth. // VAkK_7.45 //
The last [<s>vidyā</s>] belongs to one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>); two are called by that name [<s>vidyā</s>] because they arise from that [same] continuum;

children.text: iṣṭe śaikṣasya nokte tu vidye sāvidyasaṃtateḥ // VAkK_7.46 //
children.translated_text: they are not stated to be <s>vidyā</s> for a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), because [the learner's] continuum still has <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // VAkK_7.46 //

children.text: ādyā tṛtīyā ṣaṣṭhī ca prātihāryāṇi śāsanam /
children.translated_text: The first, third, and sixth [<s>abhijñās</s>] are the <s>prātihārya</s> (miraculous displays); the teaching [of <s>Dharma</s>]
is supreme, because of its unerring nature and because it connects [beings] with the desired fruit. // VAkK_7.47 //

children.text: ṛddhiḥ samādhiḥ gamanaṃ nirmāṇaṃ ca gatistridhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> (magical power) is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); movement and creation — movement is threefold;
for the Teacher, [it is] mind-swift; for others, [it is] also stream-like and through <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolute intention). // VAkK_7.48 //
What is created in the desire [realm] is external, comprising four <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-fields), of two kinds;

children.text: rūpāptaṃ dve tu nirmāṇacittaistāni caturdaśa // VAkK_7.49 //
children.translated_text: that obtained in the form [realm] is twofold; and those [creations] by the created minds (<s>nirmāṇa-citta</s>) are fourteen. // VAkK_7.49 //

children.text: yathākramaṃ dhyānaphalaṃ dve yāvat pañca nordhvajam /
children.translated_text: In sequence, [they are] the fruit of each <s>dhyāna</s>; two up to five; not from the higher [formless realm];

children.text: tallābho dhyānavat śuddhāttatsvataśca tato 'pi te // VAkK_7.50 //
children.translated_text: the attainment of that is like <s>dhyāna</s>; from the pure [<s>dhyāna</s>], from that itself, and also from those. // VAkK_7.50 //
Creation [is done] by one's own ground; but speaking [is done] also by the lower [ground];
only the creator [speaks] along with the Teacher; by empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), through the turning of others. // VAkK_7.51 //
There is empowerment even of one who has died, but not of one who is unstable; others [say] however, no;
at first, one [creation] by one [mind]; but when [concentration] is mastered, the reverse [obtains]. // VAkK_7.52 //
