The indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) [<s>ṛddhi</s>] is born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>); but that born of rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>) is threefold;

children.text: ṛddhirmantrauṣadhābhyāṃ ca karmajā ceti pañcadhā // VAkK_7.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>ṛddhi</s> also [arises] from <s>mantras</s> and herbs — and that born of <s>karma</s>: thus fivefold. // VAkK_7.53 //
The divine ear and eye are material <s>prasāda</s> (refined matter) of the <s>dhyāna</s> grounds;
they are <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous), always incomplete, with distant, subtle, and other [objects] as their sphere. // VAkK_7.54 //
What is distant, concealed, or subtle, and [what is] in all [directions] — the fleshly eye does not see;
since [it cannot see such] forms, the divine eye is desired.
Those who see [the range of] a two-thousandfold, three-thousandfold, and innumerable [world-system] are the <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and the Teacher [respectively];
another [divine eye] obtained through rebirth — <s>antarābhava</s> (intermediate existence) beings are not visible to that. // VAkK_7.55 //

children.text: cetojñānaṃ tu tattredhā tarkavidyākṛtaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of others' minds (<s>ceto-jñāna</s>) is indeed threefold: that which is produced by reasoning, [by] <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), and [by] practice;

children.text: jānate nārakā ādau nṛṇāṃ notpattilabhikam // VAkK_7.56 //
children.translated_text: hell-beings and others know [minds] at first; that obtained by birth does not [apply] to humans. // VAkK_7.56 //

body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, this is the seventh <s>kośasthāna</s> (chapter), called the Exposition on Knowledge (<s>Jñānanirdeśa</s>).

children.translated_text: The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) are declared to be twofold; their rebirths [are also taught];
<s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is a wholesome one-pointedness; it is the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) together with its accompaniments. // VAkK_8.1 //
Having <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application), <s>prīti</s> (rapture), and <s>sukha</s> (bliss), each successive [<s>dhyāna</s>] lacks the preceding factors;
likewise, the four formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) [attainments] are four aggregates, born from detachment from the lower grounds. // VAkK_8.2 //
They are called 'with exhausted form-perception'; together with three <s>sāmantaka</s> (preliminary stages);
in the formless [realm] there is no real existence of form; but the arising of form [there] is from mind. // VAkK_8.3 //
They are designated as [the sphere of] infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>),
and because of that [respective] practice; but due to dullness, [the fourth is] neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). // VAkK_8.4 //
Thus, the fundamental substance of <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is eightfold, and threefold in [another] way:
seven are 'savoring' (<s>āsvādana</s>), empty [of defilement], and pure; the eighth is twofold. // VAkK_8.5 //
That which is not associated with savoring, [yet] with craving, is the worldly wholesome [attainment] —
the 'pure' (<s>śuddhaka</s>); that [pure one] is savored by that [savoring]; the supramundane is without <s>āsravas</s> (contaminants). // VAkK_8.6 //

In the first [<s>dhyāna</s>], five [factors]: <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application), <s>prīti</s> (rapture), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration);
in the second, a group of four factors: <s>prīti</s> and the rest, and <s>prasāda</s> (inner clarity). // VAkK_8.7 //

children.text: tṛtīye pañca tūpekṣā smṛtiḥ prajñā sukhaṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third, five: <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>sthiti</s> (stability);
in the last [<s>dhyāna</s>], four: [the feelings of] neither-pleasure-nor-pain, <s>upekṣā</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>. // VAkK_8.8 //

children.text: dravyato daśa caikaṃ ca prasrabdhi sukhamādyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: In substance, [these are] eleven; <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility) and <s>sukha</s> [are present] in the first two [<s>dhyānas</s>];

children.text: śraddhā prasādaḥ prītistu saumanasyaṃ dvidhāgamāt // VAkK_8.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is <s>prasāda</s> (clarity); <s>prīti</s> (rapture) is <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) — according to the twofold tradition. // VAkK_8.9 //
In the defiled [<s>dhyānas</s>], there is no <s>prīti</s> or <s>sukha</s>, [nor] <s>prasāda</s>, [nor] full discernment, [nor] <s>smṛti</s>;
and [there is no] purity of <s>upekṣā</s> and <s>smṛti</s>; some [say there is no] <s>prasrabdhi</s> or <s>upekṣā</s> [either]. // VAkK_8.10 //
Because it is free from eight adverse conditions, the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] is called <s>āniñjya</s> (imperturbable);

children.text: vitarkacārau śvāsau ca sukhādi ca catuṣṭayam // VAkK_8.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application), the in-and-out breaths, and the group of four beginning with <s>sukha</s> (bliss) [are the eight]. // VAkK_8.11 //
<s>Saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) [are the feelings in the <s>dhyānas</s>]; in [the state of] equanimity and non-<s>saumanasya</s>,
<s>sukha</s> and <s>upekṣā</s>; <s>upekṣā</s> [alone] is established in the [higher] <s>dhyāna</s> rebirths. // VAkK_8.12 //
The body, eye, and ear consciousnesses (<s>vijñāna</s>), and whatever gives rise to <s>vijñapti</s> (expression),

children.text: dvitīyādau tadādyāptaṃ akliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ ca tat // VAkK_8.13 //
children.translated_text: from the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] onward, that [which was] obtained in the first — it is undefiled-indeterminate (<s>akliṣṭāvyākṛta</s>). // VAkK_8.13 //
One not possessing that obtains the pure [attainment] through dispassion; through [higher] rebirth,

children.text: anāsravaṃ tu vairāgyāt kliṣṭaṃ hānyupapattitaḥ // VAkK_8.14 //
children.translated_text: the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) [attainment] through dispassion; the defiled [attainment] through decline or rebirth. // VAkK_8.14 //
From the third [<s>dhyāna</s>] onward, up and down, after an outflow-free [moment], a wholesome [mind]

children.text: utpadyate tathā śuddhāt kliṭaṃ cāpi svabhūmikam // VAkK_8.15 //
children.translated_text: arises; likewise from the pure, and also a defiled [mind] of one's own ground [arises]. // VAkK_8.15 //

children.text: kliṣṭāt svaṃ śuddakaṃ kliṣṭaṃ evaṃ cādharaśuddhakam /
children.translated_text: From the defiled, [arises] one's own pure and defiled, and likewise the pure of a lower [ground];

children.text: cyutau tu śuddhakāt kliṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ kliṣṭāttu nottaram // VAkK_8.16 //
children.translated_text: at death, from the pure, a defiled [mind arises]; but from the defiled, never a higher [mind]. // VAkK_8.16 //
The pure [attainment] is fourfold: conducive to decline (<s>hāna-bhāgīya</s>) and so on, in order:
corresponding to the arising of defilements, one's own ground, a higher [ground], and the outflow-free [path]. // VAkK_8.17 //

children.text: dve trīṇi trīṇi caikaṃ ca hāna bhāgādyanantaram /
children.translated_text: Two, three, three, and one — [these are the immediate successors] after the decline-conducive and the rest;

children.text: gatvāgamya dvidhā bhūmīraṣṭau śliṣṭai kalaṅghitāḥ // VAkK_8.18 //
children.translated_text: having entered the preliminary access (<s>anāgamya</s>), the twofold grounds — the eight are traversed without gaps [when joined]. // VAkK_8.18 //
The <s>vyutkrāntaka-samāpatti</s> (leaping attainment) goes to the dissimilar [ground] as the third [in sequence];
the <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] have only one's own and lower grounds as support; a lower [ground] is useless. // VAkK_8.19 //
By the Noble One's facing the [sphere of] nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanya</s>), at the <s>Bhavāgra</s> (Peak of Existence) there is destruction of <s>āsravas</s> (contaminants);

children.text: satṛṣṇāḥ svabhavālambāḥ dhyānaṃ sadviṣayaṃ śubham // VAkK_8.20 //
children.translated_text: [the defiled attainments] are with craving, having one's own existence as object; the wholesome <s>dhyāna</s> has six objects. // VAkK_8.20 //
The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments] do not have a lower [ground] as object when contaminated;

children.text: anāsraveṇa hīyante kleśāḥ sāmantakena ca // VAkK_8.21 //
children.translated_text: defilements are abandoned by the outflow-free [path] and also by the <s>sāmantaka</s> (preliminary stage). // VAkK_8.21 //
There are eight <s>sāmantakas</s> (preliminary stages); of these, the pure ones are [characterized by] neither-pleasure-nor-pain;

children.text: ārya cādyaṃ tridhā kecit atarka dhyānamantaram // VAkK_8.22 //
children.translated_text: and the first [<s>sāmantaka</s>] is threefold for a Noble One; some [hold that] the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> is without <s>vitarka</s> (initial application). // VAkK_8.22 //
That [intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>] is threefold, [with] neither-pleasure-nor-pain; and that is the fruit [called] <s>Mahābrahmā</s>;
the <s>samādhi</s> below has <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>; from that [intermediate dhyāna] onward, [<s>samādhi</s> is] without both. // VAkK_8.23 //
The signless (<s>ānimitta</s>) [<s>samādhi</s>] functions with the aspects of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and non-self (<s>anātma</s>) — empty of [these signs];
the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) [<s>samādhi</s> functions] with the aspects of the [remaining] truths; and beyond those — // VAkK_8.24 //
the pure and stainless [<s>samādhis</s>] — the stainless ones are the threefold gateway to liberation (<s>vimokṣa-mukha</s>);
the three further <s>samādhis</s> are called emptiness-of-emptiness (<s>śūnyatā-śūnyatā</s>) and so forth. // VAkK_8.25 //
Two [of these] take the beyond-training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) [dharmas] as object; and that of emptiness, [takes] impermanence;
the signless-of-the-signless (<s>ānimittānimitta</s>) [takes] peace as [its aspect]; by the incalculable, [it leads to] destruction. // VAkK_8.26 //
They are with-<s>āsravas</s> (contaminated), in humans; for the immovable (<s>akopya</s>), lacking seven <s>sāmantakas</s>;

children.text: samādhibhāvanā dhyānaṃ subhamādyaṃ sukhāya hi // VAkK_8.27 //
children.translated_text: the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> [has four aims]: the first, the wholesome <s>dhyāna</s>, is for the sake of bliss. // VAkK_8.27 //
For the sake of seeing, mastery, and <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), [these are] born of effort;
the <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like) [<s>samādhi</s>], which is in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, is the cultivation [that leads to] destruction of contaminants. // VAkK_8.28 //
The four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) are the antidotes to ill-will and the rest:

children.text: maitryadveṣaḥ api karuṇā muditā sumanaskatā // VAkK_8.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) [counters] hatred; and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), [and] <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) [respectively]; // VAkK_8.29 //
<s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) [counters] attachment; their aspects [are]: 'may they be happy,' 'alas, they are suffering,'
'may they rejoice!' — and [their objects are] sentient beings; but beings in the desire [realm] are [their] sphere. // VAkK_8.30 //

children.text: dhyānayormuditā anyāni ṣaṭ su kecittu pañcasu /
children.translated_text: <s>Muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) [is found] in two <s>dhyānas</s>; the others in six [grounds]; some [say] in five;

children.text: na taiḥ prahāṇaṃ nṛṣveva janyante tryanvito dhruvam // VAkK_8.31 //
children.translated_text: abandonment is not [accomplished] by them; they are produced only in humans; one necessarily possesses three [at once]. // VAkK_8.31 //
The <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) are eight: the first two are the [meditations on the] impure (<s>aśubha</s>), in the two <s>dhyānas</s>;

children.text: tṛtīyo 'ntye sa cālobhaḥ śubhārūpyāḥ samāhitāḥ // VAkK_8.32 //
children.translated_text: the third is in the last [<s>dhyāna</s>], and that is non-attachment; the wholesome formless [attainments] are concentrated [<s>samāhita</s>]. // VAkK_8.32 //
Cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is an attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), [arising] immediately after the subtlest of the subtle;
by a Noble One from one's own pure [attainment] and from a lower [ground]; emergence from it [occurs] with a mental [act]. // VAkK_8.33 //
The first [<s>vimokṣas</s>] have as objects the visible forms obtained in the desire [realm]; but those who are formless —
they belong to the <s>anvaya-jñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) class, with the higher [truths] and one's own ground, and suffering and the rest as objects. // VAkK_8.34 //
The <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery) are eight; the [first] pair is like the first <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: dve dvitīyavat anyāni punaḥ śubhavimokṣavat // VAkK_8.35 //
children.translated_text: Two [are] like the second; the others, again, are like the <s>śubhavimokṣa</s> (pure liberation). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.35 //

children.text: daśa kṛtsnāni alobhāṣṭau dhyāne 'ntye gocaraḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totalities) — eight [pertain to] non-attachment; in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, moreover, [is] the domain,
Two [are in] the desire [realm], [two in] the pure [dhyānas]; in the formless realm, [they have] their own four-<s>skandha</s> domain. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.36 //
<s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) has been explained. What is obtained through <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment) and <s>prayoga</s> (practice), however, is the remainder,
Based on the three realms, the formless [attainments] are so designated; the remainder is born among humans. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.37 //
The production of the formless [attainments] in two realms [is] through cause, <s>karma</s> (action), and innate power,

children.text: dhyānānāṃ rūpadhātau tu tābhyāṃ dharmatayāpi ca // VAkK_8.38 //
children.translated_text: But the production of the <s>dhyānas</s> in the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) [is] through those two and also through the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.38 //
The true <s>Dharma</s> of the Teacher is twofold, consisting of <s>āgama</s> (scriptural tradition) and <s>adhigama</s> (realization),

children.text: dhātārastasya vaktāraḥ pratipattāra eva ca // VAkK_8.39 //
children.translated_text: Its supporters are the expounders and the practitioners themselves. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.39 //
This <s>Abhidharma</s> has been expounded by me mostly in accordance with the established doctrine of the <s>Kāśmīra</s> <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>,

children.text: yaddurguhītaṃ tadihāsmadāgaḥ saddharmanītau munayaḥ pramāṇam // VAkK_8.40 //
children.translated_text: Whatever has been poorly grasped herein is my fault; in matters of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the sages are the authority. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.40 //

children.text: nimīlite śāstari lokacakṣuṣi kṣayaṃ gate sākṣijane ca bhūyasā /
children.translated_text: When the Teacher, the eye of the world, has closed [his eyes], and when the witnesses have for the most part perished,
This teaching has been thrown into confusion by false logicians who have not seen the truth, who are without restraint. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.41 //

children.text: gate 'tha śāntiṃ paramāṃ svayaṃbhuvi svayaṃbhuvaḥ śāsanadhūrdhareṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Now that the Self-Arisen One has gone to supreme peace, and those who bore the yoke of the Self-Arisen One's teaching [have also gone],

children.text: jagatyanāthe gaṇaghātibhirmataiḥ niraṅkuśaiḥ svairamihādya caryate // VAkK_8.42 //
children.translated_text: In this unprotected world, those whose views destroy the <s>saṅgha</s> now wander freely, unchecked. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.42 //
Thus, knowing that the Sage's teaching has its life-breath at the throat,

children.text: balakālaṃ malānāṃ ca na pramādyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ // VAkK_8.43 //
children.translated_text: And [knowing] the strength and timing of the defilements, those who seek liberation must not be negligent. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.43 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, entitled 'Exposition on Attainments' (<s>Samāpattinirdeśa</s>). //
